description: Visitors are required to wear completely enclosed shoes if participating in a cave tour, like tennis shoes, sneakers or hiking boots. Any type of sandals or shoes with any openings are NOT acceptable.

title: Bringing a Pet to Big Bend?
description: Bringing your pet to Big Bend National Park will limit some of your park explorations and opportunities. Pets are not allowed on park trails, in the backcountry, or on the river. Pets are allowed only where vehicles can go. Pets may not be left unattended

title: Operating Hours & Seasons
description: The park is normally open year-round during daylight hours. Some park facilities are closed during the winter.

title: Dangerous Highway Crossing
description: Highway 177 is 60 mph with a blind spot directly across from the house. Safely use the highway underpass to the Fox Creek Trail just south of the visitor center parking lot. Be smart, stay alive.

title: No Dogs on Beach
description: Dogs and pets are not allowed on any of the beaches in Gulf Islands National Seashore. Visit the pet rules page for information.

title: Face masks are now optional
description: As Covid-related numbers have dipped below the CDC determined High Rate of Transmission in Adams County, Mississippi, face masks are no longer required in all NPS buildings at Natchez National Historical Park. Wearing of face masks is optional.

title: Rip Current Status
description: Review rip current status prior to visiting the park.

title: Fee Stations Credit Card Only
description: Fee Stations are only accepting credit cards for the purchase of entry tickets and passes.

title: Stamp Status
description: Unfortunately, since we are not an official park yet, we do not currently have a park stamp.

title: Phones Are Not Operational
description: We continue to experience intermittent outages with our phone lines. If your call does not go through, please try again later, or try to leave us a message and we will get back to you. Thank you for your understanding.

title: Fort Pulaski Entrance Fees are Credit/Debit Only
description: The park is no longer accepting cash for entrance fees. Credit and debit cards are the only method of payment currently being accepted.

title: Tickets are required to enter Mammoth Cave
description: Reservations are strongly recommended. Reservations are the only way to ensure a spot is available for your party. Please plan accordingly by visiting Recreation.gov to secure your tickets in advance. Availability of walk-up tickets is not guaranteed.

title: Park in Progress
description: Coltsville NHP is working toward establishment and is not yet an official park. We do not have a Visitor Center and visitor services are limited. For more information please visit our Park Development and Calendar pages.

title: No Fuel Services
description: Fuel up before visiting! Agate Fossil Beds National Monument is 30-50 miles from the nearest service stations.

title: Limited Cell Phone Coverage
description: Cell phone voice and data coverage is very limited in the park and surrounding area. Free visitor WiFi is available in the visitor center.

title: Possession or use of marijuana inside Fire Island National Seashore is prohibited.
description: While New York provides for regulated possession and use of marijuana, it remains an illegal drug under federal law and enforced within National Park units.

title: Trail Alerts
description: Trail closures are reported to the North Country Trail Association. Go to their Trail Alerts page for the latest information.

title: Navigation
description: Do not rely on GPS digital navigation systems to find your way to Badlands National Park. Please note that the Visitor Center at 25216 Ben Reifel Road, Interior SD 57750 is located just off I-90.

title: What To Know Before You Visit
description: Park grounds and visitor center are open, but you're encouraged to call the visitor center at 318-926-5492 for the latest information and COVID-19 precautions before you visit.

title: Motorized Recreational Scooters Not Permitted in Park
description: For the safety and protection of visitors and park resources, motorized scooters are not permitted within the park. Any vehicles (scooters, bicycles, etc.) that are part of a ride-share program may not be left behind for pick up inside the park

title: Be Prepared for your Visit
description: Before hiking at Moores Creek, make sure to bring all your necessary medications, sunscreen, bottled water for hikes, loose fitting clothes for hiking, and any other items you may need.

title: Bicycle Use In The Monument
description: Bicycles are ONLY allowed at the following locations: 1 - On the Boca Negra Canyon paved multiuse path; bicycles must remain on the paved bike path. 2 - On the crusher fine trail that winds in and out of the park around the mesa top above Boca Negra.

title: Yockanookany Trail Section Closed to Equestrians
description: The Yockanookany section of the Natchez Trace National Scenic Trail is closed to equestrian use effective immediately, due to safety concerns with trail bridges and boardwalks. The trail will remain open to pedestrians.

title: Notice to travelers to National Cemetery
description: Due to the narrow roadway & tight turn, RVs, mobile homes, charter buses, delivery trucks, or vehicles with trailers are prohibited from the crest of Monument Hill. Check for information about parking at the Visitor Center upon your arrival.

title: RV and Tractor Trailer Parking at the Visitor Center
description: There is limited space for parking for recreational vehicles and trailers in the parking lot directly in front (south) of the visitor center. RVs are asked to not park in the lot behind the visitor center. There is no parking space for tractor trailers.

title: Federal Government Shutdown
description: During the federal government shutdown, this website will not be updated and may not reflect current conditions. The tour of the Old Post Office Tower is closed for resource protection and safety.

title: GPS Navigation Systems
description: GPS navigation systems often misdirect visitors driving to Ulysses S. Grant National Historic Site. GPS systems often route visitors to our back gate, or to the entrance for Grant's Farm (not affiliated with the NPS). Please visit our directions page.

title: Footwear in the Cavern
description: For safety, closed-toe shoes with good traction are recommended. Flip flops, sandals, and some walking shoes have little or no traction and increase the possibility of slips, trips, and falls. Watch your step and use the handrails when necessary.

title: Santa Barbara Island Dock Closed; Landings Restricted to Adjacent Rocky Ledge
description: Santa Barbara Island is open to public access, but landings are restricted to the rocky ledge adjacent to the dock. The dock is closed and is not expected to be repaired in the near future due to the severe winter storm damage.

title: Arrival by Boat
description: It is prohibited to come within 1/4 mile of the Kalaupapa shoreline. Access by boat within the quarter mile offshore park boundary requires a special use permit.

title: Garden Key Harbor Light
description: Vessel operators - the Garden Key Harbor Light is undergoing repairs and is extinguished. At this time it is unknown when the light will again be illuminated.

title: Warning about GPS Systems!
description: Vehicle Navigation Systems and GPS units may provide inaccurate information—sending drivers the wrong way on one-way roads, leading them to dead ends in remote areas, or sending them on roads which are impassable. Use the Interstate exits for wayfinding.

title: Test Alert
description: Test Alert

title: White-Nose Syndrome / Cave Permit
description: Please Do Not bring clothing or caving gear used in caves or mines outside of Lava Beds into our caves. This will help slow the spread of white-nose syndrome, a bat disease that is killing bats outside of the park.

title: Firewood ban is in effect for the park.
description: Firewood ban is in effect for the park. Only firewood from the surrounding counties of Scott, Morgan, Pickett, and Fentress, in Tennessee, and McCreary in Kentucky, can be brought into the park. Firewood is for sale or you may use dead and down wood.

title: Black Bears at Big South Fork
description: Black bears call Big South Fork NRRA home. Help keep them healthy and safe by storing all food, cooking items, feed, cosmetics and coolers properly stored when at campgrounds or in the backcountry.

title: Unmanned Aircraft
description: Launching, landing, or operating an unmanned aircraft from or on lands and waters administered by the National Park Service within the boundaries of Kalaupapa National Historical Park is prohibited. This includes model airplanes, quadcopters, and drones.

title: Be Aware of Break-ins along State Route 20
description: Prevent smashed windows and theft. Break-ins are not uncommon at trailheads along State Route 20. Remove your valuables and electronics and take associated electronic cords.

title: Southern Section of Ocean Path Closed for Repairs
description: Starting Aug 31, a section of Ocean Path will be closed for repairs from a trailhead across from the Otter Point parking lot to the trail's southern terminus.

title: Dome Fire causing minimal impacts
description: The Dome Fire is burning in the wilderness northeast of Wawona, resulting in a few trail closures. Smoky conditions are possible.

title: Waterside Drive NW closures begin Sept. 21
description: Waterside Drive NW will close between Rock Creek and Potomac Parkway and Massachusetts Avenue NW beginning Sept. 21. The closure will extend north of Massachusetts Avenue to the parkway’s northbound entrance Oct. 25. Both sections will reopen Nov. 13. Drivers should follow posted detours. For more information see: https://www.nps.gov/rocr/learn/management/record-of-determination-for-the-temporary-closure-of-certain-park-roads-at-waterside-drive-nw-for-public-safety-during-roadway-rehabilitation.htm
relatedRoadEvents: [{EF6BCC19-DD6F-42E7-8474-71CED382F7AA, Waterside Drive closures begin Sept. 21 for road reconstruction , roadevent, https://www.nps.gov/rocr/planyourvisit/conditions.htm}]

title: Sept. 20: Temporary closure on Rock Creek and Potomac Parkway
description: On September 20, from 5 am to 11 am, Rock Creek and Potomac Parkway will be closed from Shoreham Drive to Virginia Avenue NW for a permitted event.

title: Possible closures on Hwy 19 at Canyon Rim Visitor Center
description: WV Department of Highways is working on a paving project outside of Canyon Rim Visitor Center. Over the coming few days (starting September 15) the entrance to the visitor center from Rt 19 may be closed periodically. If the entrance is closed, visitors can access the visitor center by driving to the next road north (Lansing Edmond Road). Make a right turn, then turn right at the next intersection onto Fayette Station Road. Immediately bear right at the fork, then stay right at the next intersection.

title: Darrah Hall Temporary Closure Starting 9/21/2026
description: Starting September 21, Darrah Hall will be temporarily closed for electrical work on the building.

title: Northern Canal Walkway closed at 2:30pm on 9/17
description: The Northern Canal Walkway will be closed to the public beginning at 2:30pm on Thursday, September 17. If conditions allow, the walkway is planned to reopen Friday, September 18, 2026, at 9am.

title: Fire restrictions are in effect
description: Campfires are only allowed in designated fire rings at Watchman Campground, South Campground, and Lava Point Campground. Smoking near vegetation is not allowed. Fireworks are never allowed within the park.

title: Please park legally and responsibly
description: Zion has limited parking. Once parking spaces in Zion are full, visitors should park in Springdale. Please park only in designated spaces. Vehicles parked outside of designated spaces are subject to citation and towing.

title: Bridge to Maryland Heights & C&O Canal CLOSED
description: The NPS is rehabilitating the stairway connecting the Goodloe Byron Memorial Footbridge to the C&O Canal NHP towpath. The stairway will be CLOSED beginning July 27 for approximately one month while crews install the new stairwell. A shuttle with very limited space will run between C&O Canal Lock 34 and Harpers Ferry NHP Visitor Center. This will impact access to Maryland Heights, the Appalachian NST, and the Potomac Heritage NST. Consider other trails.

title: Large vehicle restrictions on Zion-Mt. Carmel Highway
description: Vehicles that exceed length, width, height, or weight limits cannot travel between Canyon Junction and the park's East Entrance. See the current limits on the page linked below.

title: Toxic cyanobacteria in rivers, streams, and pools
description: Do not submerge your head in or drink instream water in Zion National Park.

title: Angels Landing Pilot Permit Program
description: All hikers need a permit to hike Angels Landing. Learn why you need a permit and how to get one using the link below.

title: Road Conditions 9/16/26
description: Conditions of county and tribal roads leading to the park have deteriorated due to recent storms. The south road (Hwy 57) is currently impassable; the north road (CR 7950) is muddy and may be impassable if the wash is flowing heavily. Chaco is also under a flood watch until 6am 9/17 - please consider current weather and your driving abilities carefully before visiting the park.

title: Road Construction on Zion-Mt. Carmel Highway
description: Nighttime closures of the Zion-Mt. Carmel Tunnel are expected between 9/21 and 9/30. When active, closures will last from 9 pm to 6 am. Check for active delays and closures on the Utah Department of Transportation website linked below. For alternative routes, visit zionarea.udot.utah.gov.

title: Stage 1 Fire Restrictions in Effect
description: Until further notice, the following are prohibited in all park areas: (1) Building, maintaining, attending, or using wood or charcoal fires anywhere but within campground- or picnic area-provided grills or grates. (The use of gas grills and camp stoves is permitted.) (2) Smoking is prohibited, except within an enclosed vehicle or while stopped in an area at least three feet in diameter that is barren of all flammable materials. (3) Discharging or using any kind of fireworks or other pyrotechnic devices.

title: North Rim Hwy 67 Closure - Sep. 16, 2026
description: As of Sep. 16 at 5:30 p.m., Hwy. 67 from Lindbergh Hill to the North Rim developed area is closed until further notice due to flooding and debris across the roadway.

title: Headquarters Visitor Center
description: Headquarters Visitor Center (elevation 7,000 ft) located 1 mile past the entrance booth will be closed beginning Thursday, September 17 for lighting and desk installation. The restrooms will remain open. Haleakalā Visitor Center (elevation 9,740 ft) will be open.

title: Partial Parking Lot Closure September 26, 2026 -Grounds/Programs Unaffected
description: Due to a construction project, half of the parking lot spots will be closed and not available for parking. Overflow parking can be found at the Paterson Museum, 2 Market Street, and the lot across the street from the Paterson Museum. We are sorry for the inconvenience.

title: Overlook Park Parking Lot - Vehicles Must Be Parked in a Designated Spot
description: Parking is extremely limited on weekends & event days. Overflow parking is available at the Paterson Museum, located at 2 Market Street. On weekends only, additional parking is available at the lot across from the Museum.

title: Temporary Closure of a Section of Bluff Trail on Lookout Mountain
description: Due to reports of aggressive wildlife, the park has temporarily closed a section of Bluff Trail, on Lookout Mountain, between the Cravens House Trail and the base of the metal staircase below Point Park. We ask that you please respect this closure and not try to hike this section of trail until the closure has been lifted. Thank you for understanding, and we apologize for any inconvenience this may cause while hiking.

title: Tsankawi Unit of Bandelier Closed Temporarily
description: The Tsankawi Unit of Bandelier will be closed from Friday, September 18 to Wednesday, September 23rd, for staging and moving of materials for a trails and visitor improvement project. Materials for this project will be staged in the parking area. A helicopter will be onsite to move the material from the parking lot to the mesa. During this time, Tsankawi will be unsafe for visitors to be in the area during this operation.

title: Increased Bear Activity in the Riverway
description: Bears have been seen approaching campsites in the Riverway in search of food. Store all food, garbage, and scented items in bear‑resistant containers, locked vehicles, or properly hung bags. Food should never be stored in tents. Stay alert and report safety concerns to 1‑800‑PARK‑TIP

title: (PEPC) Planning, Environment & Public Comment
description: Open for comment - The goal of this project is to demolish four extraneous structures at the Wright (Guinn) Farm and the Bishop Farm. The GAOA was implemented to reduce as many excess resources as possible to ensure limited funding can be directed to the most significant resources that are fundamental to the Park's mission. Significant resources include buildings in Major Battle Action Areas that provided cover and concealment or created obstacles during the Battle of Gettysburg.

title: West Nile Virus detected in Mosquito Samples at the Carrington Tract
description: West Nile Virus has been detected at the Carrington Tract from mosquito samples collected on August 31, 2026. Increased surveillance of mosquitoes in the area will continue. It is recommended visitors limit or forego outdoor activities between dusk and dawn.

title: Seboeis Road Closure 9/16 - 9/17
description: From September 16th to 17th, a portion of Seboeis Road will be closed for scheduled culvert replacement. The intersection of Swift Brook Road and Seboeis Road to Lunksoos Campground and Boat Launch is closed between 10:00 am and 4:00 pm with no thru traffic. Workers are operating heavy machinery. Visitors may detour north up Contact Station Road, returning to Lunksoos Campground and Boat Launch south via Seboeis Road. Road access to reopen on September 17th at 5:00 pm.

title: Highway Closures Will Affect Access to Popular Areas
description: In September and October of 2026, there will be a series of closures that will significantly affect trip planning for visitors to Olympic National Park. Click to see if your itinerary may need to change!

title: INNER CANYON TRAIL CLOSURES
description: Current trail closures: North Kaibab Trail, Cottonwood Campground, Phantom Ranch, Bright Angel Campground, Silver Bridge, the South Kaibab Trail below Tip-Off, and the Black Bridge. Please do not attempt to access the closed areas.

title: Please Pardon Our Dust
description: For much of September and October, the Visitor Center at Brown v. Board of Education National Historical Park will have portions of the sidewalk and courtyard closed for renovations. Visitors will still have access to the building and museum. Please be cautious of ongoing construction and follow any signs or guidance to the safest routes into the building. Accessible parking will be available in the front of the building, though it may be limited. Please call the Visitor Center with questions: 785-354-4273

title: Craters of the Moon Bookstore CLOSED on September 30
description: The Craters of the Moon bookstore and museum will be CLOSED on September 30, 2026 due to inventory. Rangers will still be available for cave permits, information, and Junior Ranger activities. Please plan accordingly.

title: Abó, Quarai, Gran Quivira Visitor Centers Delayed Opening, 9/17
description: The Abó, Quarai, and Gran Quivira Visitor Centers will open at 11AM on Thursday, September 17. The Abó, Quarai, and Gran Quivira parking lots, trails and restrooms will be open since 9AM. The Mountainair Headquarters Visitor Center will be open from 9AM to 5PM. We apologize for any inconveniences. For questions, please contact the Mountainair Headquarters Visitor Center at 505.847.2585.

title: Loop Drive mostly closed in Tucson Mountain District due to storms.
description: The following areas in the Tucson Mountain District of Saguaro National Park are closed to public use: Hohokam Road between Hugh Norris Trail Head and Golden Gate Road, and Golden Gate Road between Signal Hill Junction and Sandaro Esperanza. The closure is a result of road damage due to flash flooding on the road. Signs are in place to inform visitors of the closure. The closure will be lifted when the road is repaired, the area is safe to reenter, and the signs are removed.

title: Boston River Access
description: The Boston Store access road, limited mobility parking lot, and river landing drop-off and pick-up point will be closed on Saturday, September 19, 2026, from 7 am - 1 pm, during a public sturgeon release event.

title: 11:00 AM Ranger program Cancelled - 9/30/2026
description: The regular 11:00 AM Ranger program ("Revolutionary Roots") will be CANCELLED on Wednesday, September 30, 2026, due to a large school group that is visiting that day. The 3:00 pm will be offered as normal. We apologize for any inconvenience.

title: West Thumb Geyser Basin Boardwalk - Partial Closure
description: A section of the West Thumb Geyser Basin boardwalk will be closed to Fishing Cone and Lakeshore Geyser through mid-October while crews replace damaged support structures along the shoreline. The remaining sections of boardwalk will remain open to visitors. Dates are subject to change without notice.

title: Current East Rim Trail Status: Open
description: As of Sunday, September 13, 2026, the East Rim Trail System remains open. For more information, visit the website linked below. In good conditions the mountain bike trails are open 6 am-11 pm for bikers and as posted for other trail users. In wet or hazardous conditions, the trail will close to all users to prevent damage. Be flexible; conditions may change throughout the day.

title: Roadwork on the Gatlinburg Spur to affect traffic
description: The park will conduct single-lane closures and shoulder closures on the Gatlinburg Spur from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. September 14-17. The single-lane closures will be between the southbound section of the Gatlinburg Welcome Center and the Gatlinburg City Limits. The shoulder closures will be in the area of Huskey Grove Bridge, on both the north and southbound lanes. These closures will help the park safely conduct roadwork. Please drive with caution.

title: Fall Hunting Seasons
description: Michigan has many designated hunting seasons for different animals. Several of these hunting seasons overlap and begin mid-September. Hunting is permitted within Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore in accordance with Michigan state laws and regulations. Hunting is not permitted within 450 feet of popular sites within the park, which are listed in the Superintendent's Compendium. Wearing brightly colored clothing is recommended for visitors.

title: Hazardous Conditions at Terminus Of Aialik Glacier
description: Entering an ice fall hazard zone is prohibited in Kenai Fjords National Park. The terminus of Aialik Glacier is a high-risk area, where unstable ice can fall in blocks or columns. This can generate localized tsunami waves that wash over newly deglaciated and nearby beaches. Rapidly collapsing ice and breakage can cause severe injury or death.

title: Visitor Center will be closed on 9/16 (West Side) and 9/23 (East Side)
description: The park's visitor centers will be closing for a day this week and a day next week for WNP inventory reporting. - 9/16/26, the Red Hill Visitor Center (West District) will be closed all day. - 9/23/26, the Rincon Mountain Visitor Center (East District) will be closed all day.

title: NPS 300 Road Conditions
description: NPS 300 to Big Tubes has not been evaluated since the most recent thunderstorms. A high clearance, 4-wheel-drive vehicle is recommended. The road past Big Tubes is very rough and only accessible to high-clearance, four-wheel-drive vehicles.

title: East Portal Road temporarily closed
description: East Portal Road is temporarily closed due to intermittent weather conditions and ongoing forecasts. The road is closed to all traffic, including pedestrians and bicyclists. The closure will remain in effect until the area is safe for public access.

title: East Portal Road temporarily closed
description: East Portal Road is temporarily closed due to intermittent weather conditions and ongoing forecasts. The road is closed to all traffic, including pedestrians and bicyclists. The closure will remain in effect until the area is safe for public access.

title: Camping Restrictions Due to Wildlife Activity
description: Due to dangerous bear activity, Igloo campground is closed and Teklanika campground is restricted to camping in hard-sided vehicles only (no tents) for the remainder of the season. Backcountry units 29 and 6 are closed for at least one week for all overnight users, beginning on 9/14/26. Staff will re-evaluate and open the units when it is safe to do so. Existing campground reservations will be accommodated at another campground upon arrival and check-in.

title: Crews Responding to Mount Tom Creek Fire
description: Fire managers are responding to a lightning fire in a remote area of Olympic National Park. The Mount Tom Creek Fire has burned 69 acres 5 miles west-northwest of Mount Olympus. Firefighters are using indirect confinement tactics as part of a full-suppression strategy. Backpackers are encouraged to consider alternative routes to the Hoh River Trail should fire activity increase. There are no evacuation orders or closures.

title: Tropical Storm Edouard Impacts
description: The visitor center, trails, and waterways are open. Hikers and paddlers should be aware of fallen/leaning trees, washouts, debris, and damage to roads, trails, and bridges.

title: Site Closure – Adams Farm at Penn’s Hill
description: The Adams Farm at Penn’s Hill (John Adams and John Quincy Adams Birthplaces) is closed due to a major landscape treatment project. During construction, the entire site will be inaccessible. The Visitor Center and Peace field remain open and accessible.

title: Bag Policy
description: Bags larger than 9"x11"x5" are not permitted in the historic homes. The park does not have storage lockers for these items. Bags may not be left unattended and cannot be left with park staff. Anyone carrying a bag larger than 9"x11"x5" will not be admitted into the historic homes.

title: Park Reopened; Puʻuhonua Area and Section of Trail Remain Closed
description: Puʻuhonua o Honaunau National Historical Park has reopened following Hurricane Lowell. However, please note that the Puʻuhonua area of the park remains closed until further notice. Additionally, the 1871 Trail beyond Alahaka Ramp is also closed.

title: Empire Hill Climb: Saturday, September 19, 2026
description: The 2026 Empire Hill Climb will take place on Saturday, September 19, 2026. Drivers will race south on Wilco Rd from downtown Empire all the way to the Empire Bluff Trailhead area. Access to the Empire Bluff Trailhead will be limited. An alternative hike of similar terrain and distance is the Pyramid Point Trail to the overlook.

title: INNER CANYON WATER SHUTOFFS
description: Beginning Sep. 6, no potable water will be available in the inner canyon, including along the Bright Angel Trail (1.5 Mile Resthouse, 3-Mile Resthouse, Havasupai Gardens day use and campground). All backpackers and hikers should carry water filtration and treatment OR carry all water with them.

title: WILDFIRE CLOSURES: Sunrise & northern trails. White River open.
description: Due to several active fires on the north side of the park, the following closures are in effect until further notice: Grand Park area & trails, Northern Loop Trail, Wonderland Trail from Carbon River Suspension Bridge to Frozen Lake, & associated backcountry campgrounds. White River Road & WR Campground reopened along with White River/Sunrise Trails. Sunrise Rd CLOSED to vehicles; open for pedestrians/bicycling only.

title: Elevator is Out-of-Service
description: The elevator at the Visitor Center is currently out-of-service, due to regularly scheduled maintenance. We apologize for the inconvenience and encourage visitors to visit the virtual tours available on our website.

title: North Beach and North Beach Road temporarily closed to visitors.
description: Point Reyes National Seashore has temporarily closed North Beach after a fishing vessel ran aground early on Friday, August 21st. To ensure public and responder safety during salvage operations, the closure area includes North Beach Road (aka Point Reyes Beach North), North Beach parking lot, 500 ft in all directions from the parking lot, and the area of beach in front of the parking lot.

title: Hilina Pali Road Shoulder Work Scheduled 9/14/26 to 11/19/26
description: Hilina Pali Road beyond the Maunaiki Trailhead will be closed to motorized vehicles on September 14, 2026 from 6 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Thursday for shoulder work. Hikers, bicyclists and backcountry permit holders will be given access but should expect delays while heavy machinery works on the road. The entire road will be open to all use outside of those hours including weekends and holidays. The work is expected to be complete by November 19, 2026.

title: Parking and Road Closures in New Castle
description: Expect parking restrictions and road closures in Historic New Castle starting Wednesday, September 16 through Friday, September 18. Traffic delays are likely throughout the day. Please allow extra travel time and follow posted detours and parking instructions.

title: Ironman Triathlon: Sunday, September 20, 2026
description: Road closures on September 20, 2026. The race takes place on M-22 and will have a significant impact on local traffic. M-22 will be closed between Esch Road and Frankfort until 2 pm. Lake Michigan Road will not be accessible during the race. To avoid road closures, exit Lake Michigan Road by 8:30 am via Deadstream Road, Platte Road, or M-22 northbound. Anyone in the area of Lake Michigan Road after 8:30 am cannot depart until after 2 pm.

title: North Parking Lot at Osceola Landing to Close for Bridge Construction
description: The northernmost parking lot and co-located boat ramps at Osceola Landing will close week of 9/14 as part of the Hwy 243 Osceola Bridge replacement project. The parking lot and boat ramps will be used as a staging area and river access point for construction equipment for the duration of the Hwy 243 bridge replacement project. During this time, the rest of Osceola Landing will be open for visitor use including alternative parking lots, restrooms, picnic shelters, trail, and other river access points.

title: Special Event: September 19 & 26, 2026 - Temporary Closures of Scenic Drive
description: Reef Ride Bike Days: For this special event the Scenic Drive will be closed to motor vehicles for part of the day on Saturday, September 19 and Saturday, September 26, 2026. The road will be closed to vehicles from sunrise to 3 pm to allow for bicycles and pedestrians to enjoy the road at a more leisurely pace. The main road through the park (UT highway 24) - will remain open and unaffected by this closure.

title: Burnwood Campground and Restroom Closure
description: The Burnwood group campground will be closed from October 5 through mid November due to a construction project to replace water lines. During that time restroom facilities will be closed at the Burnwood Trailhead.

title: Visitor Center Temporarily Closed
description: The Harry S Truman National Historic Site Visitor Center is temporarily closed. Effective 9/9/26. Visitors can get tour tickets at the Noland Home, at 216 North Delaware Street Independence, MO 64050 from 9 am to 5 pm.

title: Preservation Work in Progress at The Oaks
description: Preservation and rehabilitation work has begun at The Oaks, the historic home of Booker T. Washington. The project will be completed in phases, with Phase 1 focused on restoration and preservation, including exterior improvements. The Oaks remains open by reservation only. Tours are limited to maximum of 5 visitors per reservation. Large groups and walk-in tours cannot be accommodated. To make a reservation, please call (334) 727-3200 or (334) 421-3246.

title: The Oaks Tours by Reservation Only
description: The Oaks, the historic home of Booker T. Washington is open by reservation only during an ongoing preservation and rehabilitation project. Built in 1899, the Queen Anne-style home is undergoing exterior rehabilitation work. Tours are limited to a maximum of 5 visitors per reservation. Large groups and walk-in tours will not be accommodated during this time. To make a reservation, please call (334) 727-3200 or (334) 421-3246.

title: Kīpukapuaulu Trail Closed Due to Hazardous Trees and Hanging Limbs
description: Kīpukapuaulu Trail remains closed due to numerous hazardous trees and hanging limbs resulting from several recent storms. Managers are developing a plan and will reopen the trail when it is safe.

title: Temporarily Closed for Construction
description: The Council House is closed for the rehabilitation of the home’s exterior and interior and to clean the home’s historic artifacts. The building and grounds will be closed from 9:00 a.m. September 9, 2026 until 9:00 a.m. January 27, 2027

title: Kennesaw Mountain Dr. Closed to Private Vehicles, Limited Cycling Permitted
description: The road to the top of Kennesaw Mountain is now closed to private vehicles. Shuttle service to the top of the mountain is available 7 days a week for free, parking fees still apply. Cycling is now permitted to the top of the mountain in designated lane during designated hours. Cyclist Hours: Summer: 7:30–9:30 AM & 4:30–8:30 PM Winter: 7:30–9:30 AM & 4:30–6:30 PM

title: Visitor Center Closed Sundays and Mondays
description: Beginning September 12, 2026, Minuteman Missile National Historic Site will transition back to operating five days a week. Please note that we will be closed to the public on Sundays and Mondays starting September 13 and 14.

title: Bookstore Closed: September 29 and September 30
description: The Bookstore will be closed: September 29 and September 30. During this time the Visitor Center will remain open.

title: China Beach Construction & Seacliff Avenue Closures Fall - Winter 2026
description: Park's China Beach renovation of bathhouse, lower terrace, and picnic areas is in progress. See 'more' for link to Phase 3 of China Beach project below. Visitors should expect SFPUC project on Sea Cliff Avenue to impact access to China Beach. title: Closure: USS Cassin Young
description: USS CASSIN YOUNG is currently closed due to maintenance work on Pier One in the Charlestown Navy Yard. Work is continuing through September. The ship is tentatively scheduled to re-open to the public in October.

title: Reservations Only at Buffalo Point - Starting March 15, 2027
description: Starting March 15, 2027, reservations will be required for all campsites at Buffalo Point Campground, including A & E Loops. Reservations must be made through Recreation.gov (www.recreation.gov) or by calling 877-444-6777. Reservations can be made the same day or up to six months in advance. Please note that cell phone service is unreliable in these areas, so it is strongly recommended to make your reservation before arriving at the campground.

title: NPS conducting drilling on US441/Newfound Gap Road pullout
description: From September 8-17, the scenic pullout north of the Carlos Campbell Overlook on US441/Newfound Gap Road will be closed so that the national park can complete drillwork. The road will not be closed, but please use caution while driving in the area.

title: Mississippi River Visitor Center Closure
description: The visitor center will be closed from 9/15-18 (Tue-Fri) for the Science Museum of Minnesota's annual closure. We will resume normal operating hours on Saturday, September 19th. For visitor information during the closure, email miss_info@nps.gov or call 651-293-0200. Responses may be delayed.

title: Road Blocked to West Beach
description: The main road navigating to West Beach is now blocked due to construction at the railroad crossing near the intersection of North County Rd and Route 12 until September 19. Please use the alternative route to West Beach as described on the park's status page.

title: Gas pumps out of service for scheduled repairs September 9
description: The gas pumps at Big Meadows Wayside will be out of service September 9 for scheduled repairs and testing. We strongly recommend filling up your vehicle before entering the park to ensure you have plenty of fuel for your travels.

title: Winter Hours Begin September 14
description: Winter Operating Hours in effect September 14, 2026: the visitor center is open five days a week, Wednesday through Sunday, closed on Monday and Tuesday.

title: Fort Donelson NB Park Fall Hours
description: Visitor Access to Fort Donelson NB Park Lands: Pedestrian Access is from sunrise to sunset. Automobile Access to Fort Donelson NB Park Roads 8:00 am – 6:00 p.m. daily.

description: Notch Trail and all areas within 100’ of the designated trail closed while park staff are repairing the section of the Notch trail ladder that has become a safety hazard for hikers.

title: Elevator in Garfield Home is down
description: The elevator to the second level of the Garfield Home, including the presidential memorial library, is currently not working. Visitors using wheelchairs or who cannot climb stairs will be escorted to the house museum after viewing the first floor of the home to wait for the tour to finish. We apologize for this inconvenience.

title: Gorge Wall Preservation Closures Begin Fall 2026
description: Fort Pulaski's Gorge Wall interiors will undergo preservation work beginning September 2026. For your safety, follow signage and do not cross any barricades.

title: Experiencing High Temperatures in the Visitor Center
description: While planning your visit to the site please note that we are currently experiencing some high temperatures in the Visitor Center. We apologize for any inconvenience this may cause as we work to alleviate the issue.

title: Year-round Fire Restrictions in Effect
description: Smoking is prohibited except within an enclosed vehicle. Fireworks and wood fires are always prohibited. Charcoal fires only allowed in designated grills. Visit our Fire Safety page for more info.

title: Marblemount Bridge September Nighttime Closure
description: Skagit River Marblemount Bridge will be closed overnight for repairs September 14-18, Monday night-Friday morning, 8 pm-4 am. There is no access to Cascade River Road during the nighttime closure.

title: Vehicle Break-Ins
description: Vehicle break-ins have occurred at the King Canyon Trailhead, as well as at other trailheads throughout the park. Hide valuables and consider taking them with you, secure your vehicle, and report any suspicious activity. Please call 911 to report criminal activity or the Pima County Sheriff's Department Non-Emergency number at 520-351-4900.

title: Partial Trail Closure - Dunewood Trace
description: Partially open. Persistent flooding west of the campground currently limits access to the entire trail. Hikers may not always be able to traverse the full length.

title: Closure - Hobart Woodland Trail
description: Closed. The Woodland Trail is closed indefinitely, and no reopening date is available. However, the paved Oak Savannah Trail remains open.

title: Use Caution — Devil's Lake Segment
description: Hwy 113 is undergoing a repaving project. The Ice Age Trail remains open, but the Hwy 113 crossing will be temporarily closed during paving work. Expect construction vehicles and limited parking access between CTH‑DL (north side) and Solum Ln. The project is anticipated to continue through mid‑November. title: Reroute in Effect — Baraboo Segment
description: The Ice Age Trail is closed along Effinger Rd for repaving. Follow the posted detour, which directs hikers south from STH‑113 (Water St) on a paved path, then along Mill Race Dr to Manchester St. The closure is anticipated to last until October. For maps and additional details from the Ice Age Trail Alliance, follow the link below:

title: Partial Closure - Upland Trail
description: The middle boardwalk was lost due to a tree strike, making the full loop inaccessible. At this time, there is no timeline for replacement.

title: Closure - Heron Rookery Trail
description: Closed. The trail is undergoing tree removal and rerouting due to riverbank collapse. It is expected to reopen in the fall, after mosquito activity decreases.

title: Other Park Conditions and Updates
description: For more information on storm related repairs and other park conditions like beach and hiking safety visit our park status page.

title: Reroute in Effect — Emmons Creek Segment
description: A portion of the Ice Age Trail south of Stratton Lake Rd will be closed beginning September 7 for a bridge replacement, with work expected to finish by September 15. The Stratton Lake Rd parking area may also be closed for staging. Use the white‑blazed Faraway Valley Loop to bypass the closure. title: Home of FDR - Partial Closure of Rose Garden
description: The planting beds, lawns, and paths of the Rose Garden will be under construction from late March 2026 lasting through fall of 2026. This rehabilitation will restore the crisp, level character of the garden, improve access and infrastructure, and re-install historic rose and peony varieties. During this period, the Burial Site viewing area should remain available, but occasional disruptions may restrict public access. The graves, marble monument, pet graves, and sundial will not be impacted by this project.

title: Increased Bear Activity and Dryweed Island Area Closures
description: Due to unsafe bear‑human interactions, all of the Dryweed Island area's campsites, houseboat sites, and day use sites are closed. See below for a full list of sites covered by the closure. This time of year typically brings increased bear activity throughout the park. Visitors should remain bear aware and follow all food‑storage requirements.

title: No Water at Hosmer Campground
description: Water at Hosmer Campground in the Summit District is shutoff due to a waterline break. Water is available 24-hours at Headquarters Visitor Center one mile up the road. At this point we don't have an estimate for when repairs will be complete.

title: Upper Kahuku Road Closed Beyond Boot Decontamination Station
description: Upper Kahuku Road remains closed beyond the boot decontamination station due to storm damage. The Visitor Contact Station and most trails in the Kahuku Unit are now open following Hurricane Lala. Kahuku Road above the Lower Palm Trailhead is deeply rutted by the recent heavy rains. A 4WD is recommended to access areas above the Lower Palm Trailhead.

title: Green River Ferry Temporarily Out of Service
description: The Green River Ferry has temporarily suspended operation due to low water levels. Ferry service will resume once water levels rise and conditions are safe. A river forecast is available at: water.noaa.gov/gauges/03309000

title: Limited landscape accessibility on Mondays and Tuesdays
description: Until further notice, the landscape will have limited accessibility on Mondays and Tuesdays due to a painting project. Visitors will not be able to access the side or back of the building. The site is regularly closed on these days.

title: Toxic Algae Found – Blue Mesa Water Quality Advisory
description: Cyanotoxins are currently present in the Iola Basin. Until further notice, the park recommends that no person or pet swims in, or drinks from, reservoir waters in the Iola Basin. Cyanotoxins may be present in the Cebolla and Sapinero Basins. Use caution when fishing, boating, or recreating in Blue Mesa Reservoir.

title: Accessible Parking Available
description: Accessible parking is available at the George Washington Carver Museum and The Oaks. For George Washington Carver Museum, after receiving your visitor pass, enter Tuskegee University through Lincoln Gates on Booker T. Washington Boulevard. Pass Margaret Murray Washington Hall and the Kellogg Hotel and Conference Center, then turn right to the parking garage. Accessible parking for The Oaks is at 1200 West Montgomery Road. For assistance, call Sheryl Buchanan at (334) 421-3246

title: Safety Alert Hazardous Trees in the Brandywine Valley
description: Numerous trees in the Brandywine Valley are down across the roads and trails due to the recent storm. Please use caution while driving and hiking never walk directly under a tree that is hanging. Park staff is working to improve conditions.

title: Parking Lot E Closed for Construction
description: Parking Lot E is closed for construction. The park is currently working to expand this parking area, and the lot will be closed while the expansion is being built. Visitors can still access the Mary Byrd Branch Trail and Quantico Cascades Trail by following trail reroute signs and parking vehicles in Turkey Run parking area. For your safety, please follow all closures and only park in designated parking spots.

title: Temporary Closure of Park Areas at the Request of US Secret Service
description: At the request of the United States Secret Service and to ensure necessary security and safety for the adjacent White House complex and its occupants, several designated areas of President's Park will be temporarily closed from approximately 12:00 a.m. on Tuesday, September 1, 2026, until approximately 11:59 p.m. on Tuesday, September 22, 2026. For a closure map and more detailed information, please follow the link below.

title: Fire Restrictions Starting September 1, 2026
description: Due to increased fire danger, fire restrictions have been implemented parkwide. Using wood for fires in campgrounds and picnic areas is currently prohibited. Charcoal within a grill and stoves fueled by petroleum or liquid propane gas are allowed. For more information, contact the Travertine Nature Center at 580-622-7234.

title: Parts of Santa Rosa Island Closed During Wildfire Recovery
description: Santa Rosa Island reopens to limited day use on July 1. No overnight visits are allowed. Burned areas, including Water Canyon Campground, remain closed through at least October 12. Click the more link for additional information.

title: Visitor Services Temporarily Relocated to Historic Dover Hotel
description: Visitor Services have temporarily relocated to the historic Dover Hotel (Tour Stop #10) located at 101 Petty St., Dover, TN.

title: Reroute in Effect — Montello Segment
description: A portion of the Ice Age Trail and the Krakow Park parking area on the north side of the lock channel below the Montello Dam are closed during reconstruction through June 2027. Eastbound hikers should bypass the closure via the mulched path from the boat launch, then follow the dirt driveway, pass through the adjacent parking area, and turn south on Main St (Hwy 22). For maps and additional details from the Ice Age Trail Alliance, follow the link below:

title: Cave Tour Reservations
description: Advance cave tour reservations up until October 31st are available. November reservations will become available on October 1st. Reservations are strongly recommended. Reservations full? Choose a day to come to the park early in the day to purchase a same day cave tour ticket.

title: Northbound GWMP Lane Closures Between Spout Run and Route 123 Extended
description: Northbound lanes between Spout Run Parkway and Route 123 will close Mondays through Thursdays  from 9:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m.  from Aug. 10 – Sept. 17 for tree maintenance. Southbound lane closures will begin on Sept. 21 and last until Oct. 29.

title: Watchman Trail Closed
description: The Watchman Trail is closed pending repairs.

title: OSV Status
description: 9/1/26 MD open to State Line. VA South OSV fully open to 48 vehicles. The VA North OSV fishing mile is closed.

title: Government Wash and 8.0 Mile Road Seasonal Closure May 15 – September 30
description: The Government Wash campground and 8.0 Mile Road will close on May 15th to vehicle access and overnight camping to assess and manage area improvements and protect visitors and staff from extreme heat risks. The campground is anticipated to reopen for overnight stays on October 1st. It will remain open this summer to non-motorized vehicle access for daytime, non-camping related activities.

title: Trail Closures due to recent weather event
description: Wall Street and the Bryce Connector Trail (to Peekaboo Loop) are closed until further notice.

title: Visitor Pass Needed to Visit George Washington Carver Museum
description: All visitors to Tuskegee University, including those visiting the George Washington Carver Museum located on campus, are required to obtain a visitor pass before entering. This policy is part of the university's safety and security procedures. Visitor passes are issued by Tuskegee University Public Safety. Stop by the Campus Public Safety building upon arrival to receive your pass at 1103 West Montgomery Road, Tuskegee, AL 36088.

title: DeMartin Trail and Campground
description: As part of CalTrans work to develop a new highway route that is more stable and safer, they will be undertaking geotechnical drilling this fall and winter. Hikers and campers in the area will likely see and hear heavy equipment at work and hear noise associated with the drilling, which may be 24 hours/day at times. Redwood National and State Parks has worked with CalTrans to minimize the impacts to users of this area while keeping the trail and campground open and accessible.

title: Current Fire Restrictions
description: Fires are only allowed in established fire pits.

title: Howitzer and Siege Trails Closed Beginning 9/7
description: The Howitzer and Siege trails will be closed starting on 9/7 for several weeks due to bridge repairs.

title: Paving at Alley Spring Campground Beginning 9/8/2026
description: Alley Spring Campground will close for paving from Tuesday, September 8th through Monday, September 21st for paving. The closure will include the river access and the "Bluff Hole" swimming area. Floaters putting in or taking out at Alley Spring will need to use the Burr Oak river access on the other side of the river. All pre-existing reservations during the closure have been cancelled or altered and refunds issued. We apologize for the inconvenience.

title: Level 1 Fire Advisory for areas in Stehekin
description: Chelan County Sheriff's Office issued a Level 1 Fire Advisory (Get Ready) for areas in Stehekin, Stehekin Valley Road from Harlequin Bridge to High Bridge, including Company Creek Road and side roads. Visitors should be aware there is a wildfire in the area. There are park closures in effect. For park closures visit the Fire Closures page. Stehekin businesses are open and continue to welcome visitors outside of the closure areas.

title: Tent Camping Closed at Multiple East End Campgrounds
description: Due to increased human-wildlife interactions and food storage concerns, individual tent sites and group sites at Three Mile, Daisy Farm, Moskey Basin, and Caribou Island Campgrounds are currently closed. Tent and hammock camping are not permitted anywhere within the campground. Off-trail camping zones 10, 11, 12, 13, 30, 31, 32, 33, 34, 35, 36, 37, 38 are closed. Shelters remain open. Closed areas will be patrolled to ensure compliance.

title: Stage 1 Fire Restrictions are in Effect
description: Fires are only allowed within a developed recreation site or improved site, or in an approved firepan at designated river campsites. Smoking is only allowed within an enclosed vehicle, in a developed recreation site, or in an area barren of flammable material.

title: Elevated E. Coli levels - Fremont River and Sulphur Creek
description: Recent water quality testing shows elevated E. coli levels in the Fremont River and Sulphur Creek. A warning advisory has been issued by the Utah DEQ. Use caution if entering the water. Do not get water in your mouth, do not swim. Wash hands with soap and water.

title: Road Construction
description: There will be road construction at both park units starting August 31, 2026, to September 6, 2026. Temporary traffic controls will be in place, and flaggers will guide visitors. Please follow all posted traffic control devices and directions from construction personnel. Crews may adjust construction schedules to accommodate weather or operational needs.

title: Towpath Trail Improvements
description: Hunt House Trailhead to north end of Beaver Marsh boardwalk closed from Monday, August 17 at 7 am to Friday, September 18 at 5 pm. Weekdays only, open on weekends. Beaver marsh open and accessible via Ira Trailhead. Boston Trailhead to Lock 29 in Peninsula: August 24–November 20, 2026 and March 29–April 21, 2027.

title: Stay Away From Bull Elk
description: Bull elk are fast and unpredictable this time of year and can seriously injure people. If an elk charges, run. In addition to staying at least 25 yards (23 m) away from elk and bison, always stay at least 100 yards (91 m) away from bears and wolves.

title: Sulphur Banks Bridge Closed; Boardwalk is Open
description: The Sulphur Banks Bridge is damaged and closed until further notice. The Haʻakulamanu area, boardwalk and Sulphur Banks Trail are open and accessible from the west side near Steam Vents.

title: Lees Ferry Campground Partial Closure
description: The upper loop of the Lees Ferry Campground is closed for renovations. Large equipment will be paving at the Lees Ferry campground. Do not enter construction area.

title: Water Outage
description: Visitor Center Water Outage! Due to a break in the water line, water is currently unavailable at the Visitor Center, including bathrooms and drinking fountains. We apologize for the inconvenience and appreciate your patience while repairs are underway. We’ll provide an update when water service has been restored. Please plan accordingly if you are visiting the area. We recommend bringing 32oz of water per person for a cave visit.

title: Good Luck Road Parking Lot Closed
description: The Good Luck Road Parking Lot is closed. Please use the main entrance located at 6565 Greenbelt Road, Greenbelt, MD 20770.

title: Trail Maintenance Underway Near Sand Cave
description: Crews are using Ridge Trail from Hensley to Sand Cave Trail to complete trail work. Trails remain open; some sections may be muddy or messy.

title: Bison are in the Breeding Season
description: A reminder that bison are going about their normal life cycle and may be more aggressive. A raised tail is a warning sign and the animal may charge or give chase. Please give a wide distance, at least 100 yards. There are other trails you may choose to hike without encountering the bison.

title: Auto-Theft Warning - Only Bring What You Need to the Park
description: You can prevent vehicle break-ins in parking lots and scenic overlooks. Before leaving your car for even a short period of time: 1) Remove all valuables, 2) Lock your doors. 3) Take your wallets, purses, backpacks, keys, key fobs, cell phones, and electronics with you. Read article for more details.

description: You can help prevent vehicle break-ins in parking lots. Before leaving your car to catch the ferry: 1) Remove all valuables, 2) Lock your doors. 3) Take your wallets, purses, backpacks, keys, key fobs, cell phones, and electronics with you. Read article for more details.

title: Abrams Falls Trail Closed
description: Abrams Falls Trail is closed Mondays-Thursdays through September 30 to replace aging footlog bridges and improve visitor safety. The trail will open to hikers Fridays-Sundays and on Labor Day during construction.

title: Increased Logging Traffic Along Swift Brook Road
description: Be alert for logging trucks along Swift Brook Road between the monument boundary and the start of the Loop Road. Logging trucks will be transporting logs on Swift Brook Road to Roberts Road. Logging trucks ALWAYS have the right of way. Keep your headlights on. Never stop on roads or bridges. Pull over to the side of the road to allow trucks to pass by.

title: Schoodic Mountain Road Closed for Repairs
description: Starting Aug 31, the Schoodic Mountain Road will be closed for repairs from Schoodic Loop Road to the summit of Schoodic Head. Workers will be operating heavy equipment for resurfacing, regrading and ditching.
relatedRoadEvents: [{96A00261-453A-467D-A1D5-24D68A59AB50, Schoodic Mountain Road Closed for Repairs, roadevent, https://www.nps.gov/acad/planyourvisit/conditions.htm}]

title: Pennsylvania Memorial Observation Deck Closed
description: A renovation project for the nearby Comfort Station requires electrical service to be shut off. This shut off affects lighting in the spiral staircase leading up to the Pennsylvania Memorial observation deck. The staircase is now too dark to maintain visitors’ safety. The observation deck will remain closed until the Comfort Station project is complete in early-to-mid November. Note: The base of the Pennsylvania Memorial remains open to visitation during this time.

title: Water Safety Alert
description: After recent storms, E. coli levels are likely to reach above safe swimming standards. Entering the water after heavy rainfall is never recommended. Know before you go and always check our Beach Safety page before heading to park beaches.

title: Beat the Heat
description: Make sure to take hot weather into consideration. Carry water and use sunscreen to reduce the risk of heat injuries during your visit.

title: Temporary Road Closures in Effect
description: The following roads are temporary closed: West Border Road (Roosevelt Reservation) from the Lukeville Port of Entry west to Quitobaquito Springs, East Border Road (Roosevelt Reservation) from the Lukeville Port of Entry east to the Santa Rosa Mountains, and Camino de Dos Republicas. See Alerts for more info.

title: Road Closure: Sunset Crater Volcano September 21 through October 21
description: Beginning September 21, Forest Road 545 will close to all vehicle traffic starting near the intersection with Highway 89A to the Sunset Crater Volcano entrance kiosk for culvert work. Sunset Crater Volcano National Monument remains OPEN and accessible via Forest Road 545 through Wupatki National Monument. Plan for extra travel time—the drive between visitor centers is about 19 miles/30 minutes. The road is expected to reopen October 22.

title: Road Closure: Sunset Crater Volcano September 21 through October 21
description: Beginning September 21, Forest Road 545 will close to all vehicle traffic starting near the intersection with Highway 89A to the Sunset Crater Volcano entrance kiosk for culvert work. Sunset Crater Volcano National Monument remains OPEN and accessible via Forest Road 545 through Wupatki National Monument. Plan for extra travel time—the drive between visitor centers is about 19 miles/30 minutes. The road is expected to reopen October 22.

title: South Shore Quinault Road Washed Out Beyond Park Boundary
description: South Shore Road – which is maintained by Jefferson County – is closed due to a major wash-out. For more information, visit the Jefferson County website.

title: No Water Available at the Clarno Unit
description: There is currently no water available at the Clarno Unit of the park. Please plan accordingly and bring water when visiting.

title: Great Sand Dunes Currently at Stage 1 Fire Restrictions
description: As of August 18th, Great Sand Dunes is under Stage 1 Fire Restrictions. All wood and charcoal fires must be in established fire rings in designated campsites or picnic sites. No other open fires are allowed. Fires MUST BE put out COLD before leaving your site and must not be left unattended. camp stoves and other pressurized gas devices allowed.

title: Manzanar Remains Open During US 395 Pavement Project
description: CalTrans begins a monthslong pavement project on US 395 adjacent to Manzanar National Historic Site on Monday, May 11, 2026. Crews will be working to ensure access to Manzanar remains open, but it will be important to travel cautiously as typical access may involve detours and map apps may be inaccurate. Though work is scheduled only during weekdays, lane closures and detours will be in place throughout the week. Currently, the site may only be accessed via the south entrance.

title: America the Beautiful Passes Temporary Unavailable
description: At this time all sales of America the Beautiful Passes are temporary unavailable. Please check https://store.usgs.gov/recreational-passes for locations. We will advise when passes are available for sale. We apologize for any inconvenience.

title: Food-Conditioned Bear in Arrigetch Peaks
description: On August 13, 2026 a brown bear entered camps and food caches in the Arrigetch Peaks area, obtaining food from a soft-sided, bag-type Bear Resistant Food Container (BRFC). At this time, we strongly recommend hard-sided BRFCs for all visitors to the Arrigetch Peaks area. Hard-sided BRFCs can be checked out at the Bettles Ranger Station. Backpackers in the area should maintain a high level of bear awareness and continue to follow best practices for camping in bear country.

title: Harmful Algal Blooms Occurring in Lake Richie and Intermediate Lake
description: Blooms are tested for toxin levels and monitored. Toxin levels are consistently low on Isle Royale. It is not recommended to filter water in any areas where there is surface scum, strong odors, or other evidence of a significant bloom. Blooms move around depending on wind and rain – filter water from places where blooms are not present or a different water source. It is low risk to filter water from relatively clear areas of an impacted water source.

title: Island Mine Campground Stream Low
description: The stream has very little water flow. Campers should bring enough water to Island Mine or plan on collecting water at Carnelian Beach to the south.

title: Gauley Tailwaters Campground Closure
description: The Tailwaters Campground in Gauley River National Recreation Area, located below Summersville Dam, will temporarily close from September 11 through September 28 in order to allow for more parking and better river access during the busy Gauley season.

title: Open Season
description: Jumonville Glen, Mount Washington Tavern, and the Picnic Area are OPEN until October 31st. Jumonville Glen and the Picnic Area are open daily sunrise to sunset, and Mount Washington Tavern is open every day 10 am to 4 pm.

title: Farmington Landing CLOSED
description: The National Park Service is imposing a temporary closure of Farmington Landing. This temporary closure is necessary to provide for visitor safety during a comprehensive rehabilitation project to restore park resources and improve the visitor experience. Work will include resurfacing the parking lot, replacing parking barriers, replacing trash cans with new wildlife-proof trash cans, and installing new fishing rod holders. The National Park Service appreciates the public’s cooperation in this matter.

title: Fort Foote CLOSED
description: The National Park Service is imposing a temporary closure of Fort Foote Park. This temporary closure is necessary to provide for visitor safety during a comprehensive rehabilitation project to restore park resources and improve the visitor experience. Work will include resurfacing the parking lot and gravel roadway, replacing parking barriers, removing the abandoned restroom facility and reseeding the area, and replacing trash cans with new wildlife-proof trash cans.

title: Seasonal Closure: Bush Key
description: Visitors may only access the harborside of Bush Key through Fall 2026 to protect nesting Sooty Terns, Brown Noddies, and Magnificent Frigatebirds. Boaters must maintain a distance of 100 feet from the island's mean low tide.

title: Carter G. Woodson Home NHS temporarily closed — will Reopen November 2026
description: The Carter G. Woodson Home National Historic Site is temporarily closed due to a full renovation project. The Grand Reopening of the site will take place on Saturday, November 7, 2026. Please continue to visit the website for future updates.

title: Burn Ban in Park
description: Due to high fire danger, Hot Springs National Park has enacted a BURN BAN, August 15, 2026. Only gas and charcoal grills are currently allowed for use in the campground and picnic areas.

title: Closure of Billy Mitchell Airport for Repaving Project
description: The Billy Mitchell Airport (HSE) is closed to accommodate a runway pavement rehabilitation project. The project will provide full resurfacing of paved areas, new reflective paint, and new tie-downs and anchors, improving visitor safety and enhancing the overall visitor experience.

title: Reroute in Effect — Skunk and Foster Lakes Segment
description: A reroute is in effect between Indian Valley Rd and Grenlie Rd from September 1, 2026 to January 5, 2027 due to private hunting. Bypass the closure by heading southwest, then south on N Foley Rd, and turning east on Grenlie Rd. The section between Grenlie Rd and Rieben Rd is also closed during the 9‑day gun deer season. For maps and additional details from the Ice Age Trail Alliance, follow the link below:

title: Reroute in Effect — Thornapple Creek Segment
description: The first 0.4 miles east of Thornapple Creek Rd are closed September 1–December 31 for private hunting. Bypass the closure by heading west, then south on Thornapple Creek Rd, and turning east on Gold Dust Rd. For maps and additional details from the Ice Age Trail Alliance, follow the link below:

title: Restrooms Closed
description: Castle Clinton restrooms are closed due to a maintenance issue. At the moment, we are not able to determine when they will reopen. Additional public restrooms are available in Battery Park and at the Staten Island Ferry Terminal.

title: A.G Gaston Motel Closed for Construction
description: The 1954 wing of the A.G. Gaston Motel is closed for renovation. Visit the Temporary Visitor Center in the Birmingham Civil Rights Institute at 520 16th St N, Birmingham, AL 35203 open Wednesday–Friday 10 am to 4 pm. The construction is expected to take 18 months. When completed the site will increase accessibility with a new elevator, new exhibits to tell the story of the building and Project C, and revitalize this historic landmark. Follow the link for more information.

title: Fort Spokane boat launch & day use open; Campground open with some closures
description: Fort Spokane Campground has re-opened to the public with minimal closures as of 8/14/2026. Sites 39, 40, 41, 50, and walk-in sites 64-68 will remain closed for the foreseeable future due to fire damage and hazard trees. Caution tape and closure signs have been posted for visitor safety. Please remain in open areas of the campground only. The Fort Spokane day use area and boat launch remain open. Please continue to use caution throughout these areas.

title: Temporary Location - Selma Welcome Center Closed
description: Our temporary location for the Selma Interpretive Center is closed until further notice. The Lowndes and Montgomery Interpretive Centers are open Monday through Saturday from 9:00 AM to 4:30 PM. For additional information, call us at (334)877-1983 or click "more>" below.

title: Hart Mine Road Closed
description: Hart Mine Road Closed.

title: Hyde Street Pier Closure
description: Hyde Street Pier and access to historic ships will be closed to public until further notice starting 11/04/2024 in preparation for Hyde Street Pier renovation work. Limited public access to the ships is available on Saturdays and Sundays at Mare Island.

title: Selma Interpretive Center Closed
description: The Selma Interpretive Center will remain closed to the public due to major renovations; project completion is expected in 2028. There are two other unaffected visitor centers offering services: Montgomery Interpretive Center (1521 Harris Way, Montgomery, AL 36106) Lowndes Interpretive Center (7002 US-80, Hayneville, AL 36040)

title: Reroute in Effect — Algoma Connecting Route Segment
description: A reroute is in effect on the connecting route south of Algoma. The bridge over Three Mile Creek on Longfellow Rd is closed to all travel. Bypass this closure via 9th Rd and STH‑42; note that the 10th Rd bridge is also closed. This 2.7‑mile alternate route replaces 2.8 miles of connecting route. For maps and additional details from the Ice Age Trail Alliance, follow the link below:

title: Reroute in Effect — Sturgeon Bay Segment
description: A 0.1‑mile section of the Ice Age Trail between S Neenah Ave and W Yew St is closed indefinitely. Bypass this closure via S Neenah Ave and W Yew St. This 0.5‑mile alternate route replaces 0.5 miles of Ice Age Trail. For maps and additional details from the Ice Age Trail Alliance, follow the link below:

title: Use Caution — Tisch Mills Segment
description: Flooding may occur between Mill Rd. and Nuclear Rd., especially in spring or after heavy rain. A bypass is available via CTH‑B between CTH‑BB and Nuclear Rd. For maps and additional details from the Ice Age Trail Alliance, follow the link below:

title: Reroute in Effect — Monticello Segment
description: The Stewart Tunnel is closed indefinitely pending reconstruction. The Ice Age Trail is closed at both intersections of Tunnel Rd. Follow Tunnel Rd to bypass the closure and remain on the designated alternate route. For maps and additional details from the Ice Age Trail Alliance, follow the link below:

title: Road damage possible throughout park
description: Use caution when driving through Mojave National Preserve. Widespread storms have potentially flooded or damaged roads throughout the preserve.

title: Reroute in Effect — Hartman Creek Segment
description: A reroute is in effect between the Emmons Creek Fishery Area and Hartman Creek State Park due to forestry operations. Follow posted signage to remain on the designated reroute. For maps and additional details from the Ice Age Trail Alliance, follow the link below:

title: Bat Tests Positive for Rabies, Visitors Urged to Report Potential Contact
description: A rabid bat was found at Olympic National Park near Staircase Bridge on August 9th. At approximately 2 p.m., the bat swooped down onto an unidentified woman and was temporarily caught in her hair. This individual is at risk for rabies and should seek healthcare immediately, as well as contact the Mason County Health Department at 360-427-9670 ext. 405. More at the link.

title: Expect long delays at the Hoh Rainforest
description: Lengthy delays are likely at the Hoh Rainforest entrance station between 7:30 AM - 5 PM. Plan ahead for a 1-3+ hour wait. When the parking lot fills, traffic is metered at the entrance station. Bring what you need for a long wait, and be mindful of not blocking entrances to businesses or homes along the road.

title: Lilly Bluff Overlook Decking Replacement
description: Decking replacement is underway at Lilly Bluff Overlook and is expected to take about six weeks. The overlook will remain open, but some sections will be temporarily closed as repairs are completed.

title: Primary Phone Line is Experiencing Intermittent Service Disruptions
description: The primary phone line is experiencing intermittent service disruptions. If you are unable to reach staff, please email us at libi_information@nps.gov. Please understand that emails will not be answered immediately. The park's website will have the most up-to-date information.

title: All Backpacks Must be in Storage Area at Three Mile and Rock Harbor.
description: All backpacks must be stored in backpack storage areas at Three Mile and Rock Harbor campgrounds. All food and scented items are to be in the Food Storage Lockers. Containers should be kept in the Food Storage Locker when space allows or near the Food Storage Locker, do not store in tents.

title: Heat Alert - Temperatures May Be Higher Than Forecast
description: Actual temperatures in the park may be up to 6℉ (3 ℃) higher than forecasts provided by the National Weather Service (NWS). Temperatures in rocky, exposed areas may be up to 10℉ (6 ℃) hotter than the actual temperature. Please plan accordingly, stay hydrated, limit strenuous activity during the hottest parts of the day, and be prepared for extreme heat conditions.

title: Rend Trail Closed through December 2027
description: The Rend Trail is closed for trail Improvements that will include a new parking area, restroom, and a small picnic area overlooking Arbuckle Creek at the Minden trailhead, structural improvements to five historic railroad trestles along the trail, and full trail surface rehabilitation. Additionally, construction of a large accessible ramp over the ‘big rock’ will replace a stairway, resulting in the only fully accessible earthen surface trail located within the park.

title: Fire Ban in Effect
description: Effective Thursday, August 6 building, maintaining, attending, or using a fire, or campfire, charcoal grill, tiki torches, incense burners, candles, propane campfire, wood burning stoves, and devices using pressurized liquid or gas is prohibited. This includes the designated fire rings at South Beach. Propane fire pits are not allowed during the ban.

title: Full Burn Ban Begins August 7
description: Due to increased fire activity and dry vegetation, all campfires will be prohibited starting on August 7. This includes wilderness, backcountry, non-developed and developed areas, and coastal beaches. Propane and gas stoves are allowed, if operated at least three feet away from flammable vegetation and forest litter.

title: Ocean Beach Fire Season in Effect through October 31, 2026
description: Fires allowed ONLY in park provided concrete fire rings between Stairwells 15 and 20. Do NOT make fire rings using rocks, logs or other items. When the Bay Area Air Quality Management District declares a Spare the Air Day, NO campfires, beach fires, or outdoor grills are allowed in the park. For more information, visit the beach fire regulations link below.

title: El Calderon Trail closed for construction through September 2026
description: The El Calderon Trail and parking area are closed from August 2025 through September 2026 for a major improvement project. NPS Road 100 will remain open for local traffic only, and the Continental Divide Trail will remain open for CDT thru-hikers.

title: Smoke from Wildfires May Affect Air Quality
description: Smoke from wildfires is to be expected with active fires across the region.Take precautions when recreating outdoors when heavy smoke is present.

title: Project Safety Closure in Place Near Southernmost Groin in Buxton
description: Public access is closed for 300 feet north and south of a groin repair project site in Buxton, as well as the adjacent ocean area to the east. Surfers, swimmers, and all other recreationists should stay at least 300 feet from the southernmost groin area for safety purposes.

title: 44 Creek Bridge Failure
description: 44 creek bridge is closed due to damage identified by a Federal Highway inspection team. This bridge is north of 44 Camp, approximately 7 miles south of the Redwood Creek trailhead and about 1 mile north of the Tall Trees river crossing. All trails remain open in the area, but crossing this ravine is dangerous and not advised. Hikers should plan to take alternative routes to 44 Camp, which will add at least 3.5 miles from Redwood Creek Trailhead. Stop by a visitor center for more information.

title: Temporary Closure of the Llyod W. Smith Gallery in the Museum
description: The Llyod W. Smith Gallery will be closed temporarily due to construction. All other exhibits will remain open.

title: McQueen's Island Trail Closed Beginning August 3, 2026
description: The McQueen's Island Trail will close for a Chatham County restoration project beginning August 3, 2026.

title: Air quality impacted by wildfire smoke.
description: Smoke from regional wildfires is affecting air quality in the park. When air quality is a concern: 1. monitor air quality and smoke forecasts; 2. assess your own sensitivity to poor air quality, and the sensitivity of others in your group; 3. adjust outdoor activities as needed.

title: Current Park Closures
description: Closures may occur due to inclement weather, construction projects, or other emergency conditions. Please visit the linked page for information about current closures.

title: Smokey air from local wildfires
description: Current air quality is being influenced by local fires and can change in an instant. Check https://www.airnow.gov/ for specific air quality index (AQI) information for your favorite spot at Lake Roosevelt National Recreation Area.

title: Lindenwald Opens for 2026 Season
description: Lindenwald Tours – 2026 Season Lindenwald is open for tours Friday–Sunday at 10 AM, 11 AM, 1 PM, and 3 PM. Tours are first-come, first-served. Monday–Thursday: grounds are open, but no tours are available. Park stamps, and restrooms are available in the Visitor Center.

title: Scam Warning: Book Ferry Tickets Through Authorized Concessioner Only
description: The National Park Service is aware of fraudulent websites selling invalid ferry tickets to Fort Sumter and Fort Moultrie National Historical Park. Valid ferry tickets can only be purchased through the park's authorized concessioner at www.fortsumtertours.com. Visitors should carefully verify the website address before purchasing tickets. Tickets purchased through unauthorized websites are not valid and will not be honored.

title: Construction on North Park Road
description: Construction underway on North Park Road between Leeks Marina and Lizard Creek Campground. 15-min delays both directions 6am-9pm / 1-hour delays both directions 9pm-6am. The section of road is about 7 miles north of Colter Bay and 11.5 miles south of Yellowstone.

title: Partial Beach Closures in Place in Front of Buxton Village
description: The beachfront in front of Buxton Village is temporarily closed due to the presence of threatened oceanfront structures and Dare County's beach nourishment project. Renourished sections of beach will open to the public immediately after construction activities conclude in the areas, generally within 24 hours.

title: Juniper Lake Campground Closed
description: The Juniper Lake Campground and day use area is currently closed for maintenance and campground improvement projects. Potable water is not available in the campground. The Juniper Lake Road (access to lake and trailheads) is open. Please drive with caution as road crews and contractors may be actively working along the roadway.

title: Alternate Route for Access to Root Glacier
description: The old route to access Root Glacier is no longer safe due to unstable ground. An alternative, new route exists past the Amazon Creek. Seek information at the visitor center or news release webpage.

title: Dingmans Falls Trail, Road, and Access Closed for Bridge Replacement
description: Dingmans Falls site is closed for a bridge replacement project and trail rehabilitation. All traffic, including pedestrian, cyclist, and vehicle traffic, is prohibited on the road and trail during construction.
