title: Inaccurate Third-Party Apps
description: Some third-party hiking apps are providing inaccurate trail and safety information to users. Please use the official NPS app for accurate information.

title: River Ferry at Akers (on State Highway K) CLOSED until further notice
description: The Akers Ferry on State Highway K will not be in service until further notice.

title: South Woolum Road Closed, Alternate Route Available
description: In the interest of safety, the South Woolum Road has been closed. The Woolum launch and campground remain open.

title: Most visitors need a parking tag
description: All vehicles parking for longer than 15 minutes require a parking tag. Three tag durations are available for purchase for all vehicle sizes and types: Daily ($5), Weekly ($15), or Annual ($40).

title: Camping and Docking at Boca Chita and Elliott Keys
description: Docking at Boca Chita and Elliott Keys: $25.00 Friday - Monday and Federal Holidays Camping at Boca Chita and Elliott Keys: $35.00 per night. Payments must be made on site using the recreation.gov phone app.

title: Williams Ranch Road Closed
description: The Williams Ranch Road is currently impassable and closed to public access due to unsafe conditions.

title: Only Left Side of Diablo East and Rough Canyon Boat Ramps Are Open - Rest Are Closed
description: "Due to low water levels, only the left side of Diablo East and Rough Canyon boat ramps are open. Please use caution with Spur 406 and Spur 454 launches, as the water may be too shallow to launch most boats. To see a list of open ramps, click on ""more."""

title: Ticket Required to Hike Old Rag
description: March 1 - November 30 those wishing to hike Old Rag are required to obtain a day-use ticket before arriving.

title: Martinez Adobe
description: The Martinez Adobe, located on the western edge of John Muir’s historic orchard, is currently closed due to structural damage. It is unknown when the public will be able to enter the structure. The Muir/Strentzel mansion remains open to visitors.

title: Texas White House Complex Closure
description: On January 2, 2024 the Texas White House Complex closed so the construction phase of the Texas White House rehabilitation can begin. The LBJ Ranch driving tour remains open. Visitors can still see the school, cemetery, birthplace and showbarn.

title: Park Closures
description: From time to time the missile range that surrounds the park performs military testing that may require the closure of the park or Highway 70. Please plan your visit around upcoming military tests.

title: Arizona Off-Highway Vehicle (OHV) Requirements for Residents and Non-residents.
description: Off-highway vehicles (OHVs) are required by law to display a valid OHV decal to operate on public and state trust lands in Arizona. This includes “street legal” vehicles that meet these two requirements.

title: Florissant Fossil Beds has moved to cashless fee collection
description: Entrance fees and pass purchases must be made with a credit/debit card or payment app on a mobile device. Electronic payment reduces transaction times, saves money, and improves accountability.

title: Lower Crypt Access Subject to Safe Conditions
description: Access to the lower crypt area of the Mausoleum is subject to closure during wet and or low light conditions in the late afternoon. The main floor and the two reliquary rooms remain open during these conditions.

title: Birth Home Temporarily Closed For Repairs
description: The birth home of Martin Luther King, Jr. is temporarily closed for repairs. We apologize for any inconvenience this may cause. All other buildings at the Martin Luther King, Jr. National Historical Park remain open during regular park operating hours.

title: Route 7 from Sawmill, AZ is NOT recommended
description: Entering the park from the east at Sawmill, AZ on Route 7 is not recommended. Part of this route is UNPAVED and UNMAINTAINED. Please stay on paved roads, such as Indian Route 64 from Tsaile, AZ and Highway 191/Route 7 from Chinle, AZ.

title: "Uber, Lyft, and Other ""Taxi"" Services"
description: Bandelier is in a remote location, with cell service in the canyon limited to Verizon 4G only. Services like Uber and Lyft will bring you here, but there may be no way to contact a ride out. Please plan your pickup before being dropped off at Bandelier.

title: The Use of GPS is NOT Recommended
description: Numerous visitors have been routed to remote trailheads and out-of-the-way roads trying to use GPS to reach the main park area or shuttle stop.

title: Marsh-Billings-Rockefeller National Historical Park is Cashless
description: Tours may be purchased online (recreation.gov) or in person with a credit or debit card only. Cash transactions are not available at the park.

title: CCC Camp Picnic Pavilions Closed
description: The pavilions in the CCC Camp Picnic Area are closed for the immediate future for restoration work.

title: Planning Ahead for Transportation
description: If being dropped off at the park, please ensure you will have a return ride. Taxis and rideshares do not often come out to Congaree, and the bus may be unavailable. Please plan ahead.

title: Smith Public Use Cabin Closure
description: The Superintendent issued a closure of the Smith/40-Mile Public Use Cabin due to being unsafe for public occupancy as a result of structural damage caused by the 2023 Yukon River break-up and flooding.

title: Ride Share Services
description: Convoy Point grounds, Jetty Trail, kayak launch, and picnic area open at 7 a.m. and close at 5:30 p.m. If you are using a ride share service for transportation to and from the park, ensure ride share services can be onsite before closing time.

title: Pozo Nuevo Road to Bates Well Ranch High Clearance, 4-Wheel Drive Only
description: High Clearance, 4-wheel drive is required from where Pozo Nuevo Road begins along South Puerto Blanch Drive to Bates Well Ranch area. The road is washed out in areas. Bates Well Ranch is still accessible from the north on Darby Well Road.

title: Be aware of changing beach conditions
description: Beach conditions are changing frequently. Check current tide charts and weather forecasts before traveling on the beach.

title: Jefferson Memorial elevator
description: The elevator from the ground level to the chamber of the Jefferson Memorial may be intermittently out of order. Visitors can take steps, but if you require an elevator for a successful visit, please call this number for current status: 202-426-6841.

title: Vehicle Break-in and Theft Warning
description: Car break-ins in Cuyahoga Valley have tripled since 2022, resulting in theft of personal items like credit cards. Do not leave valuables in your car. As a last resort, lock items in your trunk before arriving. Thieves target parking lots regularly.

title: Spring Creek (Queens) Closed to the Public
description: Spring Creek is closed to the public at this time. The NPS is conducting field investigations as part of a Remedial Investigation at the site. Spring Creek is located in Queens, NYC.

title: All Tickets are First-Come, First Served; We Cannot Take Reservations
description: All tickets to the Truman Home and the Truman Farm Home are first-come, first-served. At this time, we are unable to take any reservations for groups. No tickets are issued at the Truman Home itself...all tickets issued at the visitor center.

title: Navigation Warning
description: Some navigation systems on devices misdirect visitors driving to Wilson’s Creek National Battlefield. Please note that the entrance to the park is at the visitor center located near the Southeast intersection of Hwy ZZ and FR 182.

title: 4-wheel drive recommended for beach driving
description: 4-wheel drive is recommended if driving on North and South Beach.

title: Hawai'i Wildfires
description: NPS.gov information page set up for wildfires in Hawai'i.

title: Drive Cautiously - Endangered Birds on Roadway
description: Nēnē (Hawaiian geese) and ʻuaʻu (Hawaiian petrel) are nesting in the park and may land on or frequent park roads, parking lots, and road leading up to the park. Drivers are reminded to drive at the posted speed limits and exercise caution.

title: Auto-Theft Warning - Only Bring What You Need to the Park
description: You can help prevent vehicle break-ins in parking lots. Before leaving your car to catch the ferry: 1) Remove all valuables, 2) Lock your doors. 3) Take your cell phones and electronics with you. Read article for more details.

title: Auto-Theft Warning - Only Bring What You Need to the Park
description: You can prevent vehicle break-ins in parking lots and scenic overlooks. Before leaving your car for even a short period of time: 1) Remove all valuables, 2) Lock your doors. 3) Take your cell phones and electronics with you. Read article for more details.

title: Auto-Theft Warning - Only Bring What You Need to the Park
description: You can prevent vehicle break-ins in parking lots and scenic overlooks. Before leaving your car for even a short period of time: 1) Remove all valuables, 2) Lock your doors. 3) Take your cell phones and electronics with you. Read article for more details.

title: Auto-Theft Warning - Only Bring What You Need to the Park
description: You can prevent vehicle break-ins in parking lots and scenic overlooks. Before leaving your car for even a short period of time: 1) Remove all valuables, 2) Lock your doors. 3) Take your cell phones and electronics with you. Read article for more details.

title: Limited Cell Phone Coverage
description: Cell phone voice and data coverage is very limited in the park and surrounding area.

title: Fire Closures - Trail, Area, and Camp Closures
description: For closures due to fire activity visit the Fire Closures page, including trail, area, and camp closures for current and post fire conditions.

title: Rideshare services should be used with caution if visiting the Tucson Mountain District
description: Rideshare services will drop visitors off at the park, but usually will not pick them back up. To avoid being stranded in the park, coordinate two-way trips before using rideshares to visit the West side. No major trails start at the visitor center.

title: Wildlife Viewing Guidelines
description: San Juan Island National Historical Park provides habitat for many species of animals. When you visit the park, you are visiting their home. Do not approach any wildlife within 75 ft/23 m (two school bus lengths).

title: Partial Trail Closure at Portage Lakefront and Riverwalk
description: Closed portion of Portage Lakefront and Riverwalk Trail along Burns Waterway due to unsafe conditions from erosional damage. This trail portion will remain closed while funding is sought for repair work. Pier access remains open on either side of closure.

title: See TRSite.org for the latest updates on the tour schedule.
description: See TRSite.org for the latest updates on the tour schedule.

title: Kalawao County Restrictions
description: Access to the park, including Kalawao County, the Kalaupapa Trail, the settlement, and Waikolu Valley, is restricted to residents and visitors with approved permits issued by Hawaii State Department of Health. Violations will result in arrest/fine.

title: Health and Safety
description: Masks are not required but are strongly recommended for all Museum visitors. Children under the age of 5 are not permitted on in-person building tours, but are welcome to attend a neighborhood walking tour or visit us virtually.

title: Mount Tamalpais State Park - Trail Conditions
description: Many trails in Muir Woods connect to trails in Mount Tamalpais State Park. For up-to-date information about trail conditions within State Park boundaries, check the Mount Tamalpais State Park Info page (click more) and scroll down to Trail Updates.

title: The Steeple Building Closed
description: The Steeple Building remains closed until further notice.

title: County Line Road Closed Monday To Friday
description: County Line Road is closed during the week, from Monday through Friday. The closure will apply to all vehicular, pedestrian, and bicycle traffic. Please find an alternate route.

title: Roosevelt Campobello International Park is located in Welshpool.
description: Campobello Island is located in the province of New Brunswick, Canada. The physical address for the Visitor Centre is: 459 Route 774 Welshpool, New Brunswick, Canada E5E 1A4

title: Passaic River Trail Bridge washed out
description: Tropical Storm Ida washed out the Passaic River bridge on the Patriot's Path Trail south of Tempe Wick Road. This area is a known habitat of the endangered wood turtle, so do not wade, walk, or let your dog run in the river at this location.

title: Diablo Lake Boat Launch Inaccessible to Powerboats
description: Due to silt accumulation, the Diablo Lake boat launch at Colonial Creek South Campground is not usable for launching most powerboats. Expect shallow or no water at the launch ramp and the possibility of needing to carry your boat to or from the water.

title: SEASONAL SAFETY MESSAGE
description: Be careful and safe while out in the canyon! Be cautious of your surroundings, don't cliff jump, don't stray off of the main trails, and don't get too close to Little River Falls or the canyon rim. These activities could result in injury or death.

title: Fort Davis NHS is a NO DRONE Zone!
description: The use of drones is prohibited at Fort Davis National Historic Site. Thank you for preserving the cultural landscape.

title: Fort Davis NHS is in the Central Time Zone
description: Fort Davis National Historic Site is located in the Central Time Zone. The park is open 8:00 am until 5:00 pm (Central Time). The Visitor Center closes at 4:30pm. The Main Gate locks at 5:00pm.

title: Toxic Cyanobacteria in the Virgin River and the streams of Zion National Park
description: Do not submerge your head in or filter drinking water from still or moving water.

title: Dogs Not allowed on ocean beaches in Jamaica Bay and Sandy Hook March 15- Sept. 15
description: Dogs are not allowed on ocean beaches at Sandy Hook between March 15 through September 15. Dogs are not allowed on the ocean beaches at Jacob Riis Park, Fort Tilden, Breezy Point Tip and at the bayside of Breezy Point between March 15 through September 15

title: Temporary Blackland Prairie Trail Closure to Equestrians
description: Heavy rain has undermined a culvert making it unsafe for passage. Due to horse trailer parking availability, the entire section is closed to equestrians. Hikers are still able to travel from the railroad tracks to the Parkway Visitor Center.

title: Avoid area around the church & under trees in high wind conditions
description: In high wind conditions (sustained winds of 25 mph and above) visitors are advised to avoid the area around the church, with the possibility of falling clay tiles from the roof, and the cemetery, possibility of falling tree branches or limbs. Thank you.

title: Special Use Permits
description: Special Use Permits are typically needed for activities that benefit a specific group. Examples include: Groups of 40 or more, trips organized by scouting groups, churches, or academic institutions, photography, weddings, and first amendment activities

title: Weather Advisory and Storm Warnings
description: The park may have delayed openings or closures in the event of severe weather. Travel may not be recommended during these times. Please check local weather forecasts. We appreciate your understanding.

title: Weather Advisory and Storm Warnings
description: The park may have delayed openings or closures in the event of severe weather. Travel may not be recommended during these times. Please check local weather forecasts. We appreciate your understanding.

title: Weather Advisory and Storm Warnings
description: The park may have delayed openings or closures in the event of severe weather. Travel may not be recommended during these times. Please check local forecasts. We appreciate your understanding.

title: Wind Cave moves to cashless fee collection
description: Payments for cave tours, campground fees, as well as Interagency Passes at Wind Cave National Park, will be by credit/ debit cards or digital payments only. Cash and check payments will no longer be accepted.

title: Be Aware of Illegal Traffic
description: Smuggling and/or illegal entry is common in this area due to the proximity of the international border. Please be aware of your surroundings at all times and do not travel alone in remote areas.

title: The North Shoreline is Closed
description: The shoreline is closed permanently for resource protection and visitor safety.

title: Big Bend is a NO DRONE Zone
description: The use of drones is prohibited in Big Bend National Park. Thank you for preserving the peace and tranquility of Big Bend.

title: Devil's Hall is a Strenuous Hike
description: The hike to Devil's Hall is rated as strenuous. The portion of the route in the wash requires rock scrambling and is dangerous when wet or if water is present. The wash surface is loose gravel and rocks and may be unstable.

title: Oakland Main House Self-Guided Tours
description: The interior of the Oakland Main House is ONLY open to the public on weekends from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. All tours of the house are self-guided and occupancy within the building is limited. Please plan accordingly.

title: Park Operations Altered Due to Pretty Rocks Landslide
description: Summer access to facilities and services in Denali remains altered due to the Pretty Rocks Landslide and the associated closure of the Park Road at Mile 43. Check here for more information on what to expect.

title: Boater Awareness
description: Please use caution in park waters due to navigational markers that may be missing or moved due to unforeseen circumstances.

title: Appropriate Footwear Required for Cave Tours
description: Visitors are required to wear completely enclosed shoes if participating in a cave tour, like tennis shoes, sneakers or hiking boots. Any type of sandals or shoes with any openings are NOT acceptable.

title: Bringing a Pet to Big Bend?
description: Bringing your pet to Big Bend National Park will limit some of your park explorations and opportunities. Pets are not allowed on park trails, in the backcountry, or on the river. Pets are allowed only where vehicles can go. Pets may not be left unattended

title: Operating Hours & Seasons
description: The park is normally open year-round during daylight hours. Some park facilities are closed during the winter.

title: Dangerous Highway Crossing
description: Highway 177 is 60 mph with a blind spot directly across from the house. Safely use the highway underpass to the Fox Creek Trail just south of the visitor center parking lot. Be smart, stay alive.

title: No Dogs on Beach
description: Dogs and pets are not allowed on any of the beaches in Gulf Islands National Seashore. Visit the pet rules page for information.

title: Face masks are now optional
description: As Covid-related numbers have dipped below the CDC determined High Rate of Transmission in Adams County, Mississippi, face masks are no longer required in all NPS buildings at Natchez National Historical Park. Wearing of face masks is optional.

title: Rip Current Status
description: Review rip current status prior to visiting the park.

title: Fee Stations Credit Card Only
description: Fee Stations are only accepting credit cards for the purchase of entry tickets and passes.

title: Stamp Status
description: Unfortunately, since we are not an official park yet, we do not currently have a park stamp.

title: Phones Are Not Operational
description: We continue to experience intermittent outages with our phone lines. If your call does not go through, please try again later, or try to leave us a message and we will get back to you. Thank you for your understanding.

title: Fort Pulaski Entrance Fees are Credit/Debit Only
description: The park is no longer accepting cash for entrance fees. Credit and debit cards are the only method of payment currently being accepted.

title: Tickets are required to enter Mammoth Cave
description: Reservations are strongly recommended. Reservations are the only way to ensure a spot is available for your party. Please plan accordingly by visiting Recreation.gov to secure your tickets in advance. Availability of walk-up tickets is not guaranteed.

title: Park in Progress
description: Coltsville NHP is working toward establishment and is not yet an official park. We do not have a Visitor Center and visitor services are limited. For more information please visit our Park Development and Calendar pages.

title: No Fuel Services
description: Fuel up before visiting! Agate Fossil Beds National Monument is 30-50 miles from the nearest service stations.

title: Limited Cell Phone Coverage
description: Cell phone voice and data coverage is very limited in the park and surrounding area. Free visitor WiFi is available in the visitor center.

title: Possession or use of marijuana inside Fire Island National Seashore is prohibited.
description: While New York provides for regulated possession and use of marijuana, it remains an illegal drug under federal law and enforced within National Park units.

title: Trail Alerts
description: Trail closures are reported to the North Country Trail Association. Go to their Trail Alerts page for the latest information.

title: Navigation
description: Do not rely on GPS digital navigation systems to find your way to Badlands National Park. Please note that the Visitor Center at 25216 Ben Reifel Road, Interior SD 57750 is located just off I-90.

title: What To Know Before You Visit
description: Park grounds and visitor center are open, but you're encouraged to call the visitor center at 318-926-5492 for the latest information and COVID-19 precautions before you visit.

title: Motorized Recreational Scooters Not Permitted in Park
description: For the safety and protection of visitors and park resources, motorized scooters are not permitted within the park. Any vehicles (scooters, bicycles, etc.) that are part of a ride-share program may not be left behind for pick up inside the park

title: Be Prepared for your Visit
description: Before hiking at Moores Creek, make sure to bring all your necessary medications, sunscreen, bottled water for hikes, loose fitting clothes for hiking, and any other items you may need.

title: Bicycle Use In The Monument
description: Bicycles are ONLY allowed at the following locations: 1 - On the Boca Negra Canyon paved multiuse path; bicycles must remain on the paved bike path. 2 - On the crusher fine trail that winds in and out of the park around the mesa top above Boca Negra.

title: Yockanookany Trail Section Closed to Equestrians
description: The Yockanookany section of the Natchez Trace National Scenic Trail is closed to equestrian use effective immediately, due to safety concerns with trail bridges and boardwalks. The trail will remain open to pedestrians.

title: Notice to travelers to National Cemetery
description: Due to the narrow roadway & tight turn, RVs, mobile homes, charter buses, delivery trucks, or vehicles with trailers are prohibited from the crest of Monument Hill. Check for information about parking at the Visitor Center upon your arrival.

title: RV and Tractor Trailer Parking at the Visitor Center
description: There is limited space for parking for recreational vehicles and trailers in the parking lot directly in front (south) of the visitor center. RVs are asked to not park in the lot behind the visitor center. There is no parking space for tractor trailers.

title: Federal Government Shutdown
description: During the federal government shutdown, this website will not be updated and may not reflect current conditions. The tour of the Old Post Office Tower is closed for resource protection and safety.

title: GPS Navigation Systems
description: GPS navigation systems often misdirect visitors driving to Ulysses S. Grant National Historic Site. GPS systems often route visitors to our back gate, or to the entrance for Grant's Farm (not affiliated with the NPS). Please visit our directions page.

title: Footwear in the Cavern
description: For safety, closed-toe shoes with good traction are recommended. Flip flops, sandals, and some walking shoes have little or no traction and increase the possibility of slips, trips, and falls. Watch your step and use the handrails when necessary.

title: Please park legally and responsibly in Zion National Park and the Town of Springdale
description: Zion has limited parking space. Park only in designated stalls. Vehicles parked outside of designated stalls are subject to citation and may be towed. Once all designated parking stalls in Zion are full, visitors should park in Springdale.

title: Santa Barbara Island Dock Closed; Landings Restricted to Adjacent Rocky Ledge
description: Santa Barbara Island is open to public access, but landings are restricted to the rocky ledge adjacent to the dock. The dock is closed and is not expected to be repaired in the near future due to the severe winter storm damage.

title: Arrival by Boat
description: It is prohibited to come within 1/4 mile of the Kalaupapa shoreline. Access by boat within the quarter mile offshore park boundary requires a special use permit.

title: Garden Key Harbor Light
description: Vessel operators - the Garden Key Harbor Light is undergoing repairs and is extinguished. At this time it is unknown when the light will again be illuminated.

title: Warning about GPS Systems!
description: Vehicle Navigation Systems and GPS units may provide inaccurate information—sending drivers the wrong way on one-way roads, leading them to dead ends in remote areas, or sending them on roads which are impassable. Use the Interstate exits for wayfinding.

title: Test Alert
description: Test Alert

title: White-Nose Syndrome / Cave Permit
description: Please Do Not bring clothing or caving gear used in caves or mines outside of Lava Beds into our caves. This will help slow the spread of white-nose syndrome, a bat disease that is killing bats outside of the park.

title: Firewood ban is in effect for the park.
description: Firewood ban is in effect for the park. Only firewood from the surrounding counties of Scott, Morgan, Pickett, and Fentress, in Tennessee, and McCreary in Kentucky, can be brought into the park. Firewood is for sale or you may use dead and down wood.

title: Black Bears at Big South Fork
description: Black bears call Big South Fork NRRA home. Help keep them healthy and safe by storing all food, cooking items, feed, cosmetics and coolers properly stored when at campgrounds or in the backcountry.

title: Unmanned Aircraft
description: Launching, landing, or operating an unmanned aircraft from or on lands and waters administered by the National Park Service within the boundaries of Kalaupapa National Historical Park is prohibited. This includes model airplanes, quadcopters, and drones.

title: Be Aware of Break-ins along State Route 20
description: Prevent smashed windows and theft. Break-ins are not uncommon at trailheads along State Route 20. Remove your valuables and electronics and take associated electronic cords.

title: State Route 20 Closed MP134
description: State Route 20 is closed at milepost 134 (Ross Dam Trailhead) in both lanes. For more information click the link to the WSDOT real time map.

title: Trail Conditions - 5/30/2026
description: Due to elevated water levels on the Congaree River, portions of the Weston Lake, Oakridge, Boggy Gut, and Kingsnake Trails have areas of standing water, making trails difficult to navigate. The Boardwalk, Bluff, Firefly, and Longleaf Trails are currently fully accessible and open along their entire lengths.

title: Last tour of Court House at 2:00 PM on 5/30
description: The New Castle Court House Museum will have their last tour at 2:00 p.m. on Saturday, May 30th.

title: Visitor Center Opening at 11 am on June 1, 2026
description: Due to a planned power outage, the Robert Limbert Visitor Center will open at 11 am on Monday, June 1, 2026. Please plan accordingly.

title: Savage River Campground Partial Closure Due to Wildlife Activity
description: Loop A of the Savage River Campground, located at Mile 13 of the Denali Park Road, is currently closed due to ongoing wildlife activity in the area. The closure will remain in effect until further notice. Park managers will continue evaluating conditions to determine when the campground loop can safely reopen. Anyone with existing reservations for Savage River Campground during the closure period should contact reservedenali.com or call 866-761-6629 for information regarding reservations.

title: Current East Rim Trail Status: Open
description: As of Wednesday, May 27, 2026 the East Rim Trail System remains open. For more information, visit the website linked below. In good conditions the mountain bike trails are open 6 am-11 pm for bikers and as posted for other trail users. In wet or hazardous conditions, the trail will close to all users to prevent damage. Be flexible; conditions may change throughout the day.

title: Ford's Theatre to close for maintenance June 3 - August 31
description: The Petersen House, the Center of Experiential Learning, and the Atlantic Lobby will remain open to the public. National Park Service staff will be available at these locations to provide site tours and visitor information.

title: Status of Trail Ridge Road
description: Trail Ridge Road (U.S. Hwy 34 inside Rocky Mountain National Park) is open to through travel. Timed Entry Reservations are required for Trail Ridge Road from 9 am to 2 pm. Updates are available on the recorded Trail Ridge Road Status Line at 970-586-1222. Updates are also available on the RMNP webpage and the official RMNP social media pages.

title: No Shuttle Service
description: Shuttle Service has concluded for the season. Please plan accordingly and expect longer wait times. We appreciate your patience.

title: US-20 Railroad Crossing Blocked 6/1 - 6/5
description: US-20 will be blockaded from 6/1 - 6/5 for railroad crossing repairs at County Line Rd. Detour signs will be posted at various locations. As an alternative route, drive on Route 12 to visit park beaches and please drive safely.

title: 400 and 600 Loops at Alley Spring Campground Closed
description: Beginning Sunday 5/31/26 at 12:00 p.m. 600 loop at the Alley Spring Campground will be closed for repaving. The closure will last through Friday, 6/5/26. Closure of the 400 loop for repaving will begin on Monday, 6/1/26, and is expected to last through Wednesday, 6/10/2026.

title: Expect long lines at entrances on weekends.
description: Lengthy delays are likely at the southwest park entrance on SR706 on weekends. Check Google Maps for backup (represented by the orange/red line) at link below. Please do not block driveways or roads while in line outside the park.

title: Trail Access Barataria Preserve
description: Visitors seeking trail access throughout this weekend at Barataria Preserve should use Twin Canals Trail as the town of Jean Lafitte prepares for the Seafood Festival, which runs May 29-31. For festival details, visit www.lafitteseafoodfest.com. Festival admission is: Friday (5/29): $10; Saturday (5/30): $20; Sunday (5/31): $10.

title: Road work at El Malpais Visitor Center
description: Repaving of the El Malpais Visitor Center parking lot will occur the first week of June. The visitor center will remain open, but slight delays are possible. Please follow construction signage and directions.

title: Kaymoor Miners Trail Closure
description: From June 15 through November 19 the upper part of the Kaymoor Miners Trail (from Kaymoor Top down to the mine site at the junction with the Kaymoor Trail) will be closed Monday through Thursday due to a trail rehab project. The trail is expected to be fully open Friday, Saturday, and Sunday.

title: Heavy Traffic and High Visitation Alert
description: Pinnacles experiences extremely high visitation on weekends, holidays, and during favorable weather, especially in the spring. Expect long lines and delays between 10:00 am and 3:00 pm. If you're planning to hike the High Peaks, Condor Gulch, Balconies, or Moses Spring Trail, it’s recommended to arrive before 8:00 am (parking may fill earlier). Additionally, campground access may be temporarily delayed during peak periods of visitation when ALL incoming traffic is held.

title: Evans Campground Closure and Gifford Campground Changes
description: Due to severe weather on 5/28/2026, the following changes are in effect: Evans Campground: there is currently no power or water and the dump station is closed. The campground remains open and vault toilets are open and available. Please bring your own water. Gifford Campground: campground is open while safety crews are inspecting the area for hazard trees. A few campsites remain closed until inspections are complete.

title: Areas of Meridian Hill Park closed for repairs
description: Much of the upper level of the park is closed to rehabilitate the grass. Fountains and the reflecting pool are open but may be turned off or drained occasionally while adjustments to the water levels and further improvements occur. We expect the reflecting pool to be drained during the week of June 8 for additional work. Visit the Meridian Hill Park page for more information.

title: A Few Small Roads Closed Due to Roadway Damage and/or Repair Work
description: These roads are closed due to roadway damage during past storm events and/or repairs to roadway damage: Middle Fork Rd, South Fork Rd
relatedRoadEvents: [{'title': 'Road Closures Related to Road Damage From and/or Repairs Of Past Storm Events', 'id': 'EF614A2C-8A9A-4188-AED2-768723DD55A3', 'type': 'roadevent', 'url': 'https://www.nps.gov/seki/planyourvisit/conditions.htm'}]

title: Accessing Fort Barrancas
description: Fort Barrancas is open 9 am–4 pm Wednesday through Sunday. To access Fort Barrancas, visitors will need to enter the Naval Air station Pensacola through the west gate.

title: Phones down at Kingsley Plantation
description: As of 05/27, the phone lines are down at Kingsley Plantation. Please call the Fort Caroline Visitor Center at (904) 641-7155.

title: Delays along Davison Road
description: As of May 28, there is a road resurfacing project causing delays up to thirty minutes along Davison Road. Road work is anticipated to end June 4. Please stay alert and drive cautiously. Fern Canyon and Gold Bluffs beach remain open during this time.

title: For entrance fees, we accept digital passes and credit/debit cards
description: Digital passes or credit/debit cards are the ONLY method of payment at all fee collection areas. Pre-paid digital passes are available online and may be purchased in advance.

title: Roadwork may cause delays on US 41/Tamiami Trail
description: Current roadwork is ongoing along the park's northern boundary on US Highway 41/Tamiami Trail to raise the road for Everglades Restoration benefits. Drivers may experience up to 15-minute delays and should watch for personnel, equipment and slow downs.

title: Everglades' Current Alerts and Conditions
description: Be sure to review the Alerts and Conditions page before and during your visit for additional, up-to-date information on closures, cautions, and other current park conditions.

title: Visitor Center hours changing on June 1st
description: Starting June 1st, both visitor centers (Red Hills and Rincon Mountain) will switch to Summer Hours, opening at 8am and closing at 4pm. Trails remain open 24 hours a day, and the loop roads are open from dawn to dusk.

title: Group Reservations
description: Groups of 11 or more people should contact the Visitor Center at ADAM_Visitor_Center@nps.gov or 617-770-1175 at least two weeks in advance to arrange their visit.

title: Great Hall, Faneuil Hall Closures: June 2026
description: Due to scheduled events, the Great Hall will be closed on June 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11, 12, and 13. The Great Hall will close at 2 pm on June 24 and 25. The Visitor Center Desk on the market floor will remain open.

title: Jacob Riis Park Access Restrictions
description: Due to extremely hazardous conditions Gateway National Recreation Area has restricted access to sections of Jacob Riis Park. Erosion has created unsafe conditions from Bays 1-5, and portions of the eastern beach are closed.

title: North Beach Tip at Sandy Hook closed
description: North Beach Tip at Sandy Hook is closed to access until further notice due to nesting bird activity.

title: Do Not Handle Wildlife
description: If you see a dead bat or a bat acting strangely at the fort, please do not touch or move it. Report the location of the animal to park staff.

title: Annual Summer Closures and Restrictions in Effect
description: The 49 Palms trail along with some campgrounds, facilities, and areas have adjusted availability during the summer. For the full list of changes, please visit our Summer Closures page.

title: Intermittent Road Closures June 2nd - June 4th
description: Maintenance work on the monument entrance road will take place Tuesday, June 2 through Thursday, June 4. During this period, visitors should expect intermittent road closures and single‑lane traffic. Please plan for delays when entering the monument.

title: Water Unavailable at Hensley Settlement
description: Water is temporarily unavailable at Hensley Settlement.

title: Temporary Closure for San Mateo Restroom Renovations May - June 2026
description: Restrooms will be closed for renovation. • Milagra Trailhead CLOSED 5/26 - 5/27 • Mori Point Trailhead CLOSED 5/27 - 5/29 • Sweeney Ridge CLOSED 5/29 - 6/1. See map link below to see other restroom locations.

title: South parking lot closed to vehicles through June 30, 2026
description: The south parking lot of Greenbelt Park will be closed to vehicle access until June 30, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. The area will remain available to pedestrians.

title: Perimeter Trail closed through June 30, 2026
description: The section of the perimeter trail from the 0.8 mile marker to the 1.9 mile marker at Park Central Road will remain closed until June 30, 2026, at 11:59 p.m.

title: Upper and Lower Plaza Rehabilitation
description: The Plazas, Rotunda, and the Observation Deck of the Memorial will be inaccessible for the 2026 and 2027 seasons due to the Upper and Lower Plaza Rehabilitation. The visitor center and grounds will remain open. Thank you for your understanding.

title: Emergency Restoration Work
description: Emergency restoration work is taking place in front of the mission church as of 5/20/2026. This work will continue over the coming weeks and will impact views of the front of the church, but it is critical to preventing further damage and ensuring the long-term preservation of the mission.

title: Passenger Ferry Dock Closed; Visitors Deboard via Beach Landing
description: The ferry dock servicing the Cape Lookout Lighthouse area is closed for repairs. Visitors will deboard the ferry in front of the lighthouse. To reach the boardwalk, visitors will need to walk 5–10 minutes on soft sand. Depending on the tide, visitors may also need to walk through water.

title: Summer Hours: 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM
description: From Memorial Day through Labor Day, the Birthplace will be open from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM. The tour schedule remains the same.

title: Lake Powell Recreational Water Advisory
description: Any time that you do recreational activities (swimming, water skiing, making sand castles, etc.) on the beaches or in the waters of Lake Powell you are strongly encouraged to follow basic hygiene practices. A number of conditions can cause potential water quality issues on Lake Powell, at Lees Ferry, and on Colorado River tributaries.

title: Road work with possible delays and closures 06/10, 11, 12 and 15 2026
description: Schedule subject to change. Chipseal work on Volcano Road scheduled Wednesday June 10th, through Friday the 12th 2026 with a possible makeup of Monday the 15th. Crews will have flaggers and pilot cars for travel up and down Volcano Road. There may be delays and closures depending on work being performed. We are sorry for any inconvenience.

title: Cold Springs Campground Closure
description: Cold Springs Campground will be closed from June 1st - June 11th, 2026 for campground road construction. Reservations cannot be made during this time.

title: Seasonal Closure: Bush Key
description: Visitor access to Bush Key is suspended until Fall 2026 to protect nesting Sooty Terns, Brown Noddies, and Magnificent Frigatebirds. Boaters must maintain a distance of 100 feet from the island's mean low tide.

title: Closures: Detours; Towpath; Points of Interest
description: Multiple items are closed due to hazardous conditions or maintenance. See below for more details.

title: Billy Goat Trail Section A Closed
description: Section A of the Billy Goat Trail is closed due to rising levels of the Potomac River.

title: Marblemount Bridge June Closure
description: Skagit River Marblemount Bridge will be closed for repairs June 1-19, Monday-Friday, 8 pm-4 am. There is no access to Cascade River Road during the nighttime closure.

title: Cades Cove Loop Road is closed to motor vehicles every Wednesday
description: Cades Cove Loop Road is closed to motor vehicles every Wednesday through September 30. This allows pedestrians and cyclists to enjoy the cove without the presence of vehicles on the roadway.

title: Road Construction
description: Far View Sites and Cedar Tree Tower are closed for road improvements. Road work along the first four miles of the park road from the entrance station will begin in early summer. Delays of up to 30 minutes are possible - please check the park map before your visit. Wetherill Mesa Road has compacted gravel for 30 feet; motorcycles should take extra caution on this road.

title: Stage 2 Burn Restrictions
description: All campfires are prohibited. All outdoor fires, including, but not limited to, trash fires, charcoal fires, portable stoves, lanterns using gas, jellied petroleum, pressurized liquid fuel or fully enclosed (sheepherder type) stove and open fire branding activities are prohibited. Smoking shall be restricted to inside vehicles.

title: Update on Transponders
description: Due to some unexpected technical issues that are impacting recent transponder sales and renewals, Rocky Mountain National Park is temporarily pausing the sale and renewal of transponder devices. Updates will be posted on the park webpage.

title: Temporary hours of operation at Park Visitor Center due to Typhoon Sinlaku
description: The American Memorial Park Visitor Center is currently open Monday-Friday from 9-4 due to Typhoon Sinlaku recovery efforts. Park grounds and walking paths are accessible but visitors should use caution as there are fallen trees, stumps, and other typhoon debris.

title: Trail Closure at Scott’s Run Nature Preserve (McLean, Virginia)
description: Scott’s Run Nature Preserve in McLean, Virginia will close, beginning February 16th, for an urgent sewer project to renew and rehabilitate the Scott's Run Siphon wastewater facility. All trails and parking lots in the park are closed through July 4, 2026.

title: Trail Closure at Veterans Park at Balls Bluff (Leesburg, Virginia)
description: Veterans Park in Leesburg, Virginia, is closed for park improvements. All trails in the park are closed into late summer 2026.

title: May 30-31: Temporary closures on Rock Creek and Potomac Parkway
description: On May 30 and 31, there will be temporary closures on Rock Creek and Potomac Parkway for vegetation removal, hazardous tree pruning, trash removal, and road work. On May 30, 7 am to 3 pm, the southbound lanes will be closed from Beach Drive to P Street NW. Vehicles will be able to turn from Beach Drive onto Shoreham Drive or Cathedral Avenue. On May 31, 7 am to 3 pm, the southbound lanes will be closed from P Street to Virginia Avenue NW.

title: June 1-4: Kirby Nature Trail Parking Closed
description: The Kirby Nature Trail parking lot will be closed June 1-4 for repaving. The trail remains open; park along FM 420 for access.

title: NPS 300 Road Conditions
description: NPS 300 to Big Tubes has not been evaluated since the most recent rainfall. A four-wheel-drive vehicle is recommended.

title: CLOSED: Eight miles of paved road between Castolon and Santa Elena Canyon
description: The last 8 miles of Ross Maxwell Scenic Drive, from Castolon to Santa Elena Canyon, are currently closed due to flooding. Please use caution when traveling in the area. Updates will be provided as conditions change.

title: Be Bear Aware
description: "The park is bear habitat. There have been recent sightings of a bear near park trails and visitor areas. Never approach or offer food to a bear. Maintain a distance of at least 150 ft. If a bear approaches you, do not run or make any sudden movements. Make yourself look big; loudly and calmly tell the bear to ""go away;"" and slowly back away from the bear. Report any sightings to the nearest park ranger."

title: Major road construction on Hwy 199
description: Travelers using Highway 199 between Crescent City and Cave Junction should expect multiple traffic delays beginning as early as May due to ongoing Caltrans construction. For the most current delay and closure information—including upcoming four‑hour full closures—please check the Caltrans District 1 Road Information Bulletin for updates and follow their social media channels.

title: Bag Policy
description: "Bags larger than 9""x11""x5"" are not permitted in the historic homes. The park does not have storage lockers for these items. Bags may not be left unattended and cannot be left with park staff. Anyone carrying a bag larger than 9""x11""x5"" will not be admitted into the historic homes."

title: Be aware of floating debris on the Clear Creek Arm of Whiskeytown Lake.
description: With the reservoir being raised to full pool recently, there is a significant amount of wooden debris throughout the reservoir and most notably on the Clear Creek Arm west of Oak Bottom and below Judge Francis Carr Powerhouse. Plan like a park ranger for a safe day on the water. Click the link to learn more about water safety at Whiskeytown.

title: Impassible Soft Sand on Medano Road between Castle Creek and Crossing 1
description: Many off road capable vehicles are becoming stuck in soft sand between Castle Creek and Crossing One. Driving on the Medano Pass Primitive Road in this area is not advised.

title: Summer Hours
description: Visitor Access to Fort Donelson NB Park Lands: Pedestrian access is from dawn to dusk. Automobile access to Fort Donelson NB Park Roads is from 8:00 am - 8:00 pm.

title: Temporary Museum Closure
description: The park museum in the visitor center is temporarily closed for the installation of new exhibits. All other areas within the visitor center such as the welcome desk, theater, and bookstore will remain open during the project.

title: New 2026 Summer Season Hours
description: Beginning May 23, 2026, Washington Headquarters Museum and the Jockey Hollow Visitor Center have new hours, as follows: Open Thursday - Monday, 9:30 am - 4:30 pm. Closed Tuesday and Wednesday.

title: Algoma Connecting Route Segment — Bridge Closed
description: On the suggested connecting route south of Algoma, the bridge over Three Mile Creek on Longfellow Road is closed to all travel, including pedestrians. Use 9th Road and STH‑42 to bypass this closure. The bridge on 10th Road is also closed. This 2.7‑mile alternate route replaces 2.8 miles of connecting route.

title: Indian Creek Segment — Machinery and Parking Closure
description: Recent logging near CTH-E (15th Street) may mean heavy machinery and log piles in the area. The parking lot on CTH-E remains closed on weekdays. Stay alert. Remain on the trail. Use caution. Keep dogs leashed.

title: Hot Conditions
description: Limit strenuous hiking to early morning and late evening hours. Drink plenty of water and carry extra. Know the signs and symptoms of heat related illnesses. In case of a heat related emergency get to a cool place and seek help immediately.

title: Bacteria Levels at Arizona Hot Springs
description: Fecal bacteria in water samples taken from Arizona Hot Springs frequently reach high levels, which can transmit human diseases. To reduce health risks, the National Park Service recommends recreators limit body contact in these waters, clean after use, and to never put your head under water at hot springs. Please contact the Park at 702-293-8990 for updates on this advisory.

title: Stage 2 fire restrictions in effect
description: No setting, building, maintaining, attending, or using open fires of any kind in the park. This includes campfires and charcoal fires in Watchman Campground, South Campground, and picnic areas in Zion Canyon. Stoves fueled by petroleum or liquid propane gas are allowed. Smoking is allowed only in non-vegetated areas.

title: Katahdin Overlook Construction Closure
description: The Katahdin Overlook is currently closed for construction. Visitors are not permitted in the overlook area due to construction hazards. Construction is expected to be completed by mid-June 2026. All other locations on the Loop Road are accessible by motor vehicles seasonally and by foot year-round.

title: Navigation
description: Please do not rely upon GPS digital navigation systems to find your way to Craters of the Moon. Please note that the Robert Limbert Visitor Center at 1266 Craters Loop Road is located just off U.S. Highway 20/26/93 and is not accessed via any unpaved roads.

title: Stage 1 Fire Restrictions
description: Stage 1 fire restrictions in effect as of May 22, 2026. Use of portable gas stoves is permitted. Prohibited Actions: No open fires, No smoking outdoors within 3 feet of vegetation, No welding or similar devices, No flares, fireworks, etc.

title: Park Closed on Sunday, June 14
description: Steamtown National Historic Site will be closed to the public on Sunday, June 14 for safety and preparation needs preceding the visit of Union Pacific No. 4014. The site will reopen at 9 a.m. on Monday, June 15 and will be open from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. daily through June 30 for the visit of No. 4014. All entries from June 15-30 require a timed reservation. See our Big Boy Reunion page for more information.

title: Timed Entry Reservations Required June 15-30, 2026
description: Due to the high visitation expected during the visit of Union Pacific Big Boy No. 4014, all entries to the park at from June 15 to June 30, 2026 will require a timed reservation through recreation.gov. There is a non-refundable service charge of $1 for each reservation. Please see our Big Boy Reunion page for more information.

title: Beach safety closure in place in front of Buxton Village
description: The entire beachfront from the north end to the south end of Buxton Village is closed to public entry due to the presence of threatened oceanfront structures. The reopening of this beach is expected to occur following Dare County's beach nourishment project.

title: Trail update 5/21/26
description: Most trails are open and ready for the public. Those that remain closed are the Charleston Road/ Goudey Trail past the Cherokee Path and the portion of Cherokee Path between the stockade fort and the Charleston Road.

title: Barataria Visitor Center and Trails are Closed
description: Because of upcoming demolition and construction of the trails and Visitor Center, all trails at the Barataria Preserve and the Visitor Center are closed, with the exception of Twin Canals Trail. This is a day-use area only with no restrooms. Please join us Wednesdays and Thursdays 10:00 am - 2:00 pm for programming and guided hikes along the Wetland Trace trail at 1:00 pm at 4917 City Park Drive, Jean Lafitte, 70067.

title: Upcoming Power Outages in Bartlett Cove
description: Attention visitors, residents, and workers in Bartlett Cove and the Glacier Bay Park Headquarters area: Be aware of upcoming power outages related to local maintenance work. All lasting from approx. 9 am - 1 pm: Saturday, 5/23 - An outage will occur park-wide (all of Bartlett Cove local area). Sunday 5/24 - Outage at the park generator building, including the Bartlett Cove fuel dock. Monday 5/25 - Outage at the park maintenance building. Thursday, 5/28 - Outage at the Glacier Bay lodge.

title: Castle Williams Re-opening
description: Beginning, Saturday, May 23, 2026, Castle Williams will be open to the public, Wednesday through Sunday and Holiday Mondays, from 10am to 4pm. The America’s National Parks Bookstore and the National Parks Passport will be available in the Castle. Stay tuned for an opening announcement for Fort Jay, which will remain closed for the time being. If you have any questions, you can reach us through the contact link on this site.

title: Middle Islands Passage Buoy Off Course
description: The navigational buoy at Middle Islands Passage is off course. Use caution boating in this area until buoy can be re-set.

title: Elk with Calves are Extremely Dangerous
description: Be alert, especially this time of year around Mammoth Hot Springs. Elk calves may be hidden close to buildings, under or next to vehicles, and around blind corners. You must remain at least 25 yards from all wildlife. If an elk charges, retreat!

title: Lava Point Campground Closed
description: The Lava Point Campground is closed through June 3, 2026.

title: Denali Park Road Information
description: In summer, the Denali Park Road is open to Mile 15 (Savage River) for personal vehicles. Vehicle travel further into the park is limited to transit and tour buses.

title: 2026 Tour Season
description: Visit https://www.nps.gov/adam/planyourvisit/2026-tour-season.htm for details on the 2026 tour season, including operating hours and tour offerings. The Visitor Center is open 9am-5pm Wednesdays-Sundays. The historic homes are open Wednesdays-Sundays. Entrance fees required for entry into historic homes. Guided tour reservations are available first-come, first-served on the day of the tour at the Visitor Center. Reservations not required for self-guided tours.

title: Theodore Roosevelt House Tour Reservation Updates Beginning June 1
description: Starting June 1, 2026: All 2PM & 3PM tour tickets will be sold one day in advance at 9:30 am. A 2PM & 3PM tour will be offered on Thursdays. 12PM & 1PM tour tickets will continue to go on sale on the morning of the tour at 9:30AM. A new military discount ticket option will be available (military I.D. required). Additional details to come.

title: Stoplight In Use due to Limited Parking
description: Limited Parking at the Visitor Center is monitored by the use of a Stoplight. This light helps meter traffic so that parking spots are available for visitors. Stoplight generally in effect from 10 am to 4 pm. Wait times vary daily.

title: Stage 1 Fire Restrictions
description: Stage 1 Fire Restrictions begin May 21st. Igniting or using fires fueled by combustible materials, that create an open flame, is strictly prohibited. Smoking is only allowed within an enclosed vehicle or developed site. For details on fire restrictions, visit https://wildlandfire.az.gov/fire-restrictions

Smoking is only allowed within an enclosed vehicle or developed site. For details on fire restrictions, visit https://wildlandfire.az.gov/fire-restrictions
